definition_en: the act of judging faults, or a careful judgement of a work
core_image: 一篇文章的页边写满红笔批注
scene: 编辑把稿子退回来，页边全是红笔字。 Her criticism was sharp but useful.
sceneCN: 这里 criticism 指「批评」（第 1 个义项：指出缺点与问题的评判）；句意是她的批评尖锐但有用。

senses.title: The act of finding faults
senses.definition: the act of saying what is wrong with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人或某事哪里不对的行为
senses.example: He took the criticism calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了批评。
senses.why: A fault named clearly can be repaired.
senses.whyCN: 被清楚指出的毛病，才有机会修好。

senses.title: A judgement of a work
senses.definition: a careful written or spoken judgement of a book, play or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对书籍、戏剧或观点作出的细致评判
senses.example: She wrote a criticism of the new novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这部新小说写了一篇评论。
senses.why: Judgement can praise as well as blame.
senses.whyCN: 评判既能责备，也能称赞。

senses.title: The study of literature
senses.definition: the academic study and judgement of literary works
senses.definitionCN: 对文学作品进行的学术研究与评判
senses.example: He teaches literary criticism at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大学教文学批评。
senses.why: A whole discipline grew from the habit of judging texts.
senses.whyCN: 一整门学科，就是从评判文本的习惯里长出来的。

intro.en: Criticism joins critic, from Greek kritikos, with the suffix -ism.
intro.cn: criticism 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos）加后缀 -ism 构成。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate and to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开与判断。

items.en: Kritikos described a person able to judge.
items.cn: kritikos 形容有能力判断的人。

items.en: Criticus named the judge of a text.
items.cn: criticus 指评判文本的人。

items.en: Criticism named the work of a critic.
items.cn: criticism 指评论家所做的工作。

items.en: It also meant the pointing out of faults.
items.cn: 它也开始指指出缺点。

items.en: It now covers both blame and scholarly judgement.
items.cn: 今天它兼指责备与学术评判。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the critic- stem, and the meaning group names other acts of judging aloud.
note.cn: 形近组共享 critic- 词干，近义组列出其他公开评判的说法。

entries.definition: a person who judges works
judging, or extremely important
to point out faults
a published judgement of a new work
entries.definitionCN: 对新作品公开发表的评判

entries.definition: strong official disapproval
the feeling that something is wrong

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with red ink and end with a whole shelf of theory.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从红墨水开始，最后落到整整一架理论书。

normal.en: Critic plus -ism: the habit that a critic lives by.
normal.cn: critic 加 -ism：评论家赖以为生的那个习惯。

normal.en: Red ink on a margin is a map of what to fix.
normal.cn: 页边的红字，是一张该修哪里的地图。

normal.en: Good criticism leaves the work standing, only straighter.
normal.cn: 好的批评让作品仍站着，只是更直。

normal.en: The word can praise; blame only got there first.
normal.cn: 这个词也能称赞，只是责备先占了位置。

normal.en: A shelf of theory began with one sharp remark.
normal.cn: 一架理论书，始于一句尖锐的话。

abstract.en: Picture a page with more red than black.
abstract.cn: 想象一页红字比黑字还多的稿子。

abstract.en: Picture a polite letter that still stings.
abstract.cn: 想象一封客气却仍然刺人的信。

abstract.en: Picture a lecture hall arguing over one line.
abstract.cn: 想象阶梯教室里为一句话争论。

examples.en: She accepted the criticism without anger.
examples.cn: 她毫无怒气地接受了批评。

examples.en: The report offers useful criticism of the design.
examples.cn: 这份报告对设计提出了有用的批评。

examples.en: He is reading modern literary criticism.
examples.cn: 他正在读现代文学批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criticism 记成 critic（评论家）加 -ism：评论家干的那件事，就是评判，也包括挑毛病。

root: 由 critic（源自希腊语 kritikos，善于判断的）加 -ism 构成；本义是「评论家所做之事」，后兼指指出缺点与对作品的学术评判。

sensesIntro.en: From naming a fault, to judging a work, to a discipline built on judging.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指出一处毛病，到评判一部作品，再到建立在评判之上的学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red ink filling the margin of a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：页边被红墨水写满的稿子。

branches.en: Naming a fault is the first use of the word.
branches.cn: 指出毛病，是这个词最早的用法。

branches.en: A full judgement weighs merits as well as faults.
branches.cn: 完整的评判既称缺点，也称优点。

branches.en: The habit of judging became a field of study.
branches.cn: 评判的习惯，长成了一门学问。

branches.en: Both blame and praise are forms of judgement.
branches.cn: 责备与称赞，都是评判的形式。

branches.en: A review and a thesis can share the same method.
branches.cn: 一篇书评和一篇论文，可以用同一套方法。

intro.en: Criticism is critic plus -ism, the suffix that names a practice or a doctrine.
intro.cn: criticism 是 critic 加 -ism，这个后缀表示一种做法或主张。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back through Latin criticus to Greek krinein, to judge.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干经拉丁语 criticus 上溯到希腊语 krinein（判断）。

items.example: The critic read the draft twice.
items.exampleCN: 评论家把稿子读了两遍。

items.example: Her notes were critical but kind.

items.exampleCN: 带着判断去读这份稿子。
不加分辨的称赞帮不了任何人。

latinEntries.example: Latin criticus named the learned reader.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 criticus 指博学的读者。

definition_en: covering a large area; very great in amount; wide in range
core_image: 一片望不到边的田野铺展在眼前
scene: 这场风暴造成了广泛破坏。 The storm caused extensive damage.
sceneCN: 这里 extensive 是「大量的、大规模的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这场风暴造成了广泛破坏。

senses.title: Wide in range
senses.definition: covering a large area or range
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖大片区域或很大范围的
senses.example: The project required extensive research.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要广泛的研究。
senses.why: The core sense is a wide stretch of coverage.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是覆盖面的大幅铺展。

senses.title: Very great in amount
senses.definition: very great in amount or degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度非常大的
senses.example: The flood caused extensive damage.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水造成了大规模破坏。
senses.why: Wide range becomes great amount.
senses.whyCN: 宽广的范围变成巨大的数量。

senses.title: Covering much land
senses.definition: covering a large area of land
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖大片土地的
senses.example: The house has extensive gardens.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子有宽阔的花园。
senses.why: The stretch of space is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 空间的铺展是最早的含义。

intro.en: Extensive comes from Latin extensivus, from extendere, to stretch out.
intro.cn: extensive 来自拉丁语 extensivus，根源是 extendere（向外拉伸）。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Extensivus means tending to stretch out.
items.cn: extensivus 意为倾向于向外伸展的。

items.en: Extensive describes wide areas and large amounts.
items.cn: extensive 描述广阔区域与大量事物。

items.en: Extensive appears in research and damage.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extensive 常用于研究与破坏。

items.en: Extend, extension, and extent share the root.
items.cn: extend、extension 与 extent 共享同一词根。

note.en: Extensive means wide; intensive means deep and concentrated.
note.cn: extensive 是广泛的，intensive 则是密集深入的。

entries.definition: costing a lot of money
involving a lot of effort in a short time
showing feelings clearly
large from side to side
large in extent or range
including everything needed

normalIntro.en: Extensive describes things that spread wide or reach a great amount.
normalIntro.cn: extensive 描述铺展得很广或数量很大的事物。

normal.en: The report is based on extensive research.
normal.cn: 这份报告基于广泛的研究。

normal.en: The fire caused extensive damage to the forest.
normal.cn: 大火对森林造成了大规模破坏。

normal.en: She has extensive knowledge of local history.
normal.cn: 她对当地历史有广博的知识。

normal.en: The estate has extensive grounds.
normal.cn: 这座庄园有宽阔的场地。

normal.en: Extensive use of plastic worries scientists.
normal.cn: 塑料的广泛使用让科学家担忧。

abstract.en: Picture a field that runs far beyond sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一片一直延伸到视线之外的田野。

abstract.en: Imagine a map covered with many small marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一张布满许多小标记的地图。

abstract.en: Think of a library with shelves in every room.
abstract.cn: 想象一座每个房间都摆满书架的图书馆。

examples.en: The storm caused extensive damage to the coast.
examples.cn: 风暴对海岸造成了大规模破坏。

examples.en: They carried out extensive tests.
examples.cn: 他们进行了广泛的测试。

examples.en: The castle has extensive gardens.
examples.cn: 这座城堡有宽阔的花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: extend（延伸）加 -ive：延伸得很开的，就是 extensive（广泛的）。

root: 源自拉丁语 extensivus，由 extendere（向外拉伸）派生，核心义「铺展得很广、数量很大」。

sensesIntro.en: Extensive means wide in range, very great in amount, or covering much land.
sensesIntro.cn: extensive 意为范围广泛、数量巨大，或覆盖大片土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field stretching beyond sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：延伸到视线之外的田野。

branches.en: The base sense is wide coverage.
branches.cn: 基础义是宽广的覆盖范围。

branches.en: Wide range becomes a great amount.
branches.cn: 宽广范围变成巨大数量。

branches.en: The oldest sense is land stretched out.
branches.cn: 最早的含义是铺展开的土地。

branches.en: Wide range and large amount often go together.
branches.cn: 范围广与数量大常常相伴。

branches.en: Coverage in research and in land share the same width.
branches.cn: 研究范围与土地面积共享同一种「广」。

intro.en: Extensive is extend plus -ive, and it belongs to the same family as extension and extent.
intro.cn: extensive 由 extend 加 -ive 构成，与 extension、extent 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin extensivus and extendere are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extensivus 与 extendere 是来源形式。

items.meaning: in a wide or thorough way
items.example: The subject has been studied extensively.
items.exampleCN: 这个课题已被广泛研究。

items.example: They measured the extensiveness of the damage.
items.exampleCN: 他们评估了破坏的广泛程度。
他们建了一个扩建部分。

items.example: The extent of the damage is unknown.

items.exampleCN: 他参加了一个强化课程。

items.example: The room has an expansive view.

definition_en: an ordained religious minister, especially a Catholic or Anglican one, or an official who performs sacred rites in another religion
core_image: 祭坛前系着圣带、转过身来的黑袍身影
scene: 清晨的老教堂里，木门刚开，长椅上还留着昨夜的凉气，一位穿黑袍的人站在祭坛前把圣带系好。 The priest turned from the altar and greeted the first old woman who came in from the cold.
sceneCN: 这里 priest 指「神父」（第 1 个义项：天主教会中主持弥撒、听告解的圣职人员）；句意为神父从祭坛前转过身，向第一位进来避寒的老妇人问安。图中可辨识物件：祭坛、圣带、教堂长椅。

derivatives.zh: 由 priest 加抽象名词后缀 -hood 构成，义为「神职；司铎身份；全体神职人员」
由 priest 加表示女性的后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女祭司」
由 priest 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「神职人员的；像教士的」

senses.title: An ordained minister of the Catholic or Orthodox Church
senses.definition: a man ordained in the Roman Catholic or Orthodox Church to celebrate Mass and to hear confession
senses.definitionCN: 在天主教或东正教会中受圣职、可以主持弥撒并听告解的男子
senses.example: The priest listened to her confession for nearly an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 神父听了她近一个小时的告解。
senses.why: Greek presbyteros meant an elder of the community, and the western church kept that title for the man who stands at the altar on the people's behalf; the everyday English name for him is this word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 presbyteros 本是「团体中的长老」，西方教会把这个称号留给代表众人站在祭坛前的人，英语里对这个人最常用的称呼就是 priest。

senses.title: An ordained minister in Anglican and similar churches
senses.definition: a member of the clergy in the Church of England and churches of similar order, ranking below a bishop
senses.definitionCN: 英国国教会及同类教会中的圣职人员，位次低于主教
senses.example: The priest read the notices and then blessed the small congregation.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师念完通告，随后为这一小群会众祝福。
senses.why: Where the church kept the old ladder of deacon, priest and bishop, the middle rung kept the old name too, so an Anglican clergyman is a priest rather than a minister.
senses.whyCN: 凡保留了「会吏—司铎—主教」这套旧阶梯的教会，中间那一级也保留了旧名，所以圣公会的圣职人员叫 priest，而不叫 minister。

senses.title: An official who offers sacrifice in another religion
senses.definition: a person who performs sacred rites and offers sacrifice in a non-Christian or ancient religion
senses.definitionCN: 在非基督教或古代宗教中主持圣事、献祭的人
senses.example: A priest lit the fire before the stone image at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时，祭司在石像前点起了火。
senses.why: The word was never limited to one faith: any religion that sets aside a person to handle sacrifice and ritual gets the same English label, because the job, not the creed, is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从未只属于一种信仰：任何宗教只要专门设一个人来管献祭与仪式，英语都用同一个词，因为这个词命名的是那份职责，而不是教义。

senses.title: A clergyman as a familiar figure in a community
senses.definition: a member of the clergy spoken of informally as a local figure, especially one serving a village, a parish, or a hospital
senses.definitionCN: 对神职人员的口语统称，尤指在村庄、堂区或医院里服务的那一位
senses.example: The village priest buried three generations of the same family.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的教士安葬过同一家族的三代人。
senses.why: Once a community has one such man who baptizes, marries and buries its people, the word stops describing an office and starts naming a familiar neighbour, which is this looser fourth sense.
senses.whyCN: 当一个社区里总有这么一个人为孩子洗礼、为新人证婚、为逝者下葬，这个词就不再只是在说一个职衔，而是在说一位熟悉的邻居，这就是更宽松的第四义。

intro.en: Priest goes back to a Greek word for an older man: the church took the word for a community elder, Latin passed it on, and the Germanic languages borrowed it early enough to wear its edges smooth.
intro.cn: priest 的源头是希腊语中表示「年长者」的词：教会借它指团体里的长老，拉丁语再往下传，日耳曼诸语借得早，把词形磨得很圆。

items.en: The Greek noun presbys meant an old man or an elder, someone whose age gave him standing in the group.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 presbys 指老人、长者，年岁让他在群体里有发言的分量。

items.en: Its comparative presbyteros meant older, and the early Greek-speaking church used it for the elders who governed a congregation.
items.cn: 它的比较级 presbyteros 意为「较年长的」，早期讲希腊语的教会用它指管理会众的长老。

items.en: Latin took the title as presbyter, an elder of the church, and kept it for the second order of clergy below the bishop.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个称号接过去写作 presbyter，指教会中的长老，后来专指低于主教的第二级圣职人员。

items.en: The Germanic peoples borrowed the spoken Latin form at an early date; Old English has prēost, with the middle consonants worn down, and the word was in use long before the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 日耳曼各族很早就借用了拉丁语的口语词形；古英语里已有 prēost，中间几个辅音被磨掉，这个词在诺曼征服之前很久就在用了。

items.en: Middle English preost became modern priest, and Latin presbyter was later borrowed a second time as a learned word, so priest and presbyter are one root reached by two roads.
items.cn: 中古英语 preost 变成现代英语 priest；后来拉丁语 presbyter 又被当作学术词再借一次，所以 priest 与 presbyter 是同一个词根走了两条路。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek and Latin forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers the other English names for a religious minister.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一词根的希腊语、拉丁语词形展开；近义组收英语里对宗教圣职人员的其他称呼。

entries.definition: An elder of the early church; the Latin form was borrowed into English a second time as a learned term.
entries.definitionCN: 早期教会中的长老；这个拉丁词形后来被当作学术词再次借入英语。

entries.definition: The body of elders of a church, or the part of a church reserved for the clergy.
entries.definitionCN: 教会的长老团，或教堂中供圣职人员使用的区域。

entries.definition: Belonging to a church governed by elders rather than bishops.
entries.definitionCN: 属于由长老而非主教治理的教会的。

entries.definition: A woman who performs sacred rites, formed by adding the feminine suffix -ess.
entries.definitionCN: 主持圣事的女性，由加女性后缀 -ess 构成。

entries.definition: A member of the clergy, especially in a Protestant church.
entries.definitionCN: 圣职人员，尤指新教教会的。

entries.definition: A man who has been ordained for religious duties.
entries.definitionCN: 受圣职、担任宗教职务的男子。

entries.definition: A minister who cares for a particular congregation.
A priest in charge of a parish in the Church of England.
entries.definitionCN: 英国国教会中主管一个堂区的牧师。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek title for an elder that travelled through Latin into Old English, and its family still splits into the churchly and the scholarly branch.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语对长者的称呼，经拉丁语进入古英语，它的同族至今分成教会用语与学术用语两支。

normal.en: Presbyteros in Greek means an older man, so a priest began as the elder of a group rather than a man with a special power.
normal.cn: 希腊语 presbyteros 意为「较年长的人」，所以 priest 最初是团体里的长者，而不是拥有特殊法力的人。

normal.en: The same root gives presbyter, presbytery and Presbyterian, all of them about elders rather than altars.
normal.cn: 同一个词根给出 presbyter、presbytery 与 Presbyterian，讲的都是长老而不是祭坛。

normal.en: Old English prēost borrowed the spoken Latin form early, which is why the spelling is so far from presbyter.
normal.cn: 古英语 prēost 很早就借了口语词形，所以拼写和 presbyter 差得很远。

normal.en: The -hood in priesthood marks a state or office, as it does in childhood and brotherhood.
normal.cn: priesthood 里的 -hood 表示身份或状态，和 childhood、brotherhood 一样。

normal.en: The -ess in priestess marks a female counterpart, the same ending as in actress and goddess.
normal.cn: priestess 里的 -ess 表示女性对应者，和 actress、goddess 用法相同。

abstract.en: The word travels from age to office: first an old man, then the elder of a congregation, then the man at the altar.
abstract.cn: 这个词从年岁走向职分：先是老人，再是会众的长老，最后是站在祭坛前的人。

abstract.en: One root reaches English twice, once worn smooth as priest and once kept sharp as presbyter, like a coin and its proof.
abstract.cn: 一个词根两次抵达英语，一次磨圆成 priest，一次保持原样成 presbyter，像流通的硬币与它的样币。

abstract.en: A priest is defined by standing in for others, which is why the same word serves faiths that share no creed.
abstract.cn: priest 的关键是替别人站到前面，所以这个词能同时服务彼此毫无共同教义的宗教。

examples.en: The priest turned from the altar to greet the first visitor.
examples.cn: 神父从祭坛前转过身，向第一位来客问安。

examples.en: Her grandfather was a Catholic priest in a small mountain parish.
examples.cn: 她的祖父是山区小堂区的一位天主教神父。

examples.en: In the temple, a priest lit the fire before the stone image.
examples.cn: 庙里，祭司在石像前点起了火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里斯特」——听着像「仆里侍」：在祭坛边侍奉的人，就是 priest。

root: 希腊语 presbys（老人）→ 比较级 presbyteros（较年长的、长老）→ 拉丁语 presbyter（教会长老）→ 日耳曼语早借，古英语 prēost → 现代英语 priest。后来拉丁语 presbyter 又被直接再借一次，成为学术同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an elder who stands for the group before the sacred; the senses divide by which church is speaking, then widen to any officiant of sacrifice and to the familiar local clergyman.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「替众人站到神圣面前的年长者」；义项按说话的教会分开，再扩到任何主持献祭的人，最后落到社区里那位熟悉的教士。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in dark robes turning from the altar toward the people.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿深色长袍的身影从祭坛前转过身，面向众人。

branches.en: a black cassock turning from the altar
branches.cn: 黑袍从祭坛前转过身

branches.en: a vicar reading notices after the service
branches.cn: 礼拜结束后宣读通告的牧师

branches.en: a fire lit before a stone image
branches.cn: 石像前燃起的火

branches.en: a familiar figure at every village burial
branches.cn: 每场乡村葬礼上都出现的身影

branches.en: the same man at the altar and at the graveside
branches.cn: 同一个人在祭坛前，也在墓旁

intro.en: The word is a Greek comparative of age, its Latin church title, the worn Old English borrowing, and the English endings that name the office and its female counterpart.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语中表示年岁的比较级、拉丁语的教会称号、磨圆的古英语借词，以及命名职分与女性对应者的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Greek title entered Latin as presbyter and stayed in church use, so a Latin cognate is well recorded even though English took the word by an older spoken route.
latinIntro.cn: 这个希腊称号进入拉丁语后写作 presbyter 并一直在教会里使用，所以拉丁同族有明确记录，只是英语走的是更早的口语路径。

items.meaning: church elder, priest of the second order

latinEntries.meaning: the body of elders, the place reserved for them
latinEntries.meaningCN: 长老团；长老所在的区域

definition_en: the process of changing from one state, form, or activity to another
core_image: 闸门之间的一小段桥：从这头走到那头
scene: 毕业典礼结束，学生收拾宿舍行李，准备走向职场：秋天来了，山里的小镇正悄悄地完成从夏日旅游到滑雪季的 transition。
sceneCN: 这里 transition 是「过渡」（第 1 个义项：从一种状态到另一种状态）；句意是小镇由夏季旅游过渡到滑雪季。

collocations.zh: 从 A 到 B 的过渡

derivatives.zh: 由 transition 加 -al 构成，义为「过渡的；临时的」
由 transition 加 -ist 构成，义为「主张转型者」（罕用）
由动词加现在分词构成，义为「转型过程；身份过渡」

senses.title: A change from one state or form to another
senses.definition: the act of changing from one state, stage, or form into another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种状态、阶段或形式变为另一种
senses.example: The transition from school to work is never easy.
senses.exampleCN: 从学校到职场的过渡从来不易。
senses.why: The core image is the short bridge between two gates: you are leaving one and arriving at the other.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两道闸门之间的小桥：你既已离开一处，又正在抵达另一处。

senses.title: A period during which such change happens
senses.definition: a time during which a change of state is in progress
senses.definitionCN: 状态转变正在发生的时期
senses.example: The company set a two-year transition for the new system.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为新系统设置了两年过渡期。
senses.why: The bridge itself takes time to cross; that time is the transition.
senses.whyCN: 走完这座桥需要时间；这段时光就是过渡期。

senses.title: A smooth connection between pieces of writing or music
senses.definition: a passage connecting sections of text or music
senses.definitionCN: 连接文章或乐曲各部分的段落
senses.example: The essay needs a better transition between the two paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章两段之间需要更好的衔接。
senses.why: Writers and composers build small bridges so their readers cross without stumbling.
senses.whyCN: 作者与作曲家搭起小桥，让读者顺畅走过。

intro.en: Transition comes from Latin transitio, a going across, from transire (to go across), built on trans- (across) and ire (to go).
intro.cn: transition 来自拉丁语 transitio「走过去」，动词 transire 由 trans-（跨越）与 ire（走）构成。

items.en: ire meant to go, a root also seen in exit and transit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ire 意为「走」，也见于 exit、transit。

items.en: transire meant to go across or pass over.
items.cn: 拉丁语 transire 意为「跨过、经过」。

items.en: transitio named the passage between subjects in rhetoric.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 transitio 指修辞中的话题过渡。

items.en: Borrowed with meanings of passing and change.
items.cn: 16 世纪借入英语，意为经过与改变。

items.en: Now spans personal, political, and technical changes.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖个人、政治与技术领域的转变。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to transition, and words in the change field.
note.cn: 与 transition 形近音近的词，以及同属转变义场的词。

entries.definition: an act of doing business
entries.definitionCN: 交易，与 transition 只差词根：ire 走过去，agere 办妥

entries.definition: the act of passing through
entries.definitionCN: 运输；通行，同根词 transire 的另一派生

entries.definition: lasting only a short time
entries.definitionCN: 短暂的；瞬间的，同源形容词

entries.definition: to become different
a change of form or use
entries.definitionCN: 转变；换算，强调形式的转换

entries.definition: a change of position or direction
entries.definitionCN: 变动；转移，偏方向与重心

entries.definition: a complete change of form
entries.definitionCN: 彻底变形，强调结果的全新

normalIntro.en: Remember ire, to go: a transition is a change you walk across.
normalIntro.cn: 记住词根 ire「走」：transition 是要走过去的变化。

normal.en: trans- (across) + ition (going)
normal.cn: 跨过去（trans）+ 走（ition）＝过渡

normal.en: transit, transitory are the same family
normal.cn: transit（通行）、transitory（短暂）同属一词族

normal.en: collocation: smooth transition
normal.cn: 常用搭配 smooth transition（平稳过渡）

normal.en: transition from A to B
normal.cn: 从 A 到 B 的过渡是固定句式

normal.en: watch out for transaction
normal.cn: 勿与 transaction（交易）混淆

abstract.en: A narrow bridge between two open gates
abstract.cn: 两道敞开的闸门之间的一座窄桥

abstract.en: A chrysalis hanging: neither caterpillar nor butterfly yet
abstract.cn: 悬在枝头的蛹：既非毛虫也非蝴蝶

abstract.en: A single chord sliding the song into a new key
abstract.cn: 一个和弦让歌曲滑进新调

examples.en: The country is going through a difficult economic transition.
examples.cn: 该国正经历艰难的经济转型。

examples.en: Good writing needs smooth transitions between paragraphs.
examples.cn: 好文章需要段落间顺畅的衔接。

examples.en: The bridge will close during the transition to a new route.
examples.cn: 路线切换期间大桥将封闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹日行」——过渡期里每天踹着自己往前走一脚：踹（trans）日（ire 走）行 → transition，走着过桥的意思。

root: 拉丁语 trans-（跨越）+ ire（走）→ transire「走过去」→ transitio「跨越之行走」：一切过渡都是走过去的那一段。

sensesIntro.en: From walking across, the word covers state changes, the time they take, and the joins in art.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「走过去」延伸到状态转变、转变所需的时间与艺术中的衔接。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the short bridge between two gates
core.cn: 核心意象：两道闸门之间的一座小桥

branches.en: the change itself between states
branches.cn: 状态之间的转变本身

branches.en: the time spent changing
branches.cn: 转变所占用的时间

branches.en: the written or musical join
branches.cn: 文章或乐曲的衔接

branches.en: you cannot rush the bridge; it has its own length
branches.cn: 桥有其长度，过渡不能硬赶

branches.en: both roads and texts need smooth crossings
branches.cn: 路与文章都需要顺畅的过渡

intro.en: Transition shows the Latin pair trans- + ire, shared by transit and transitory.
intro.cn: transition 呈现了拉丁语 trans- 加 ire 的组合，与 transit、transitory 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire also gave exit, circuit, ambition (going around), and perish (going through).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ire 还派生了 exit、circuit、ambition（四处奔走）与 perish（走完全程而消亡）。

items.meaning: the passing of goods or people

latinEntries.meaning: a going across, a passing over

definition_en: a man or boy, used in a friendly informal way, or a painful crack in the skin
core_image: 一个穿着旧外套、笑着打招呼的年轻男子
scene: 门口站着一个瘦高的年轻人。 A tall chap in a grey coat asked for directions.
sceneCN: 这里 chap 指「小伙子；家伙」（第 1 个义项：对男子的非正式称呼）；句意是门口一个穿灰大衣的高个年轻人来问路。

senses.title: A man or boy
senses.definition: a man or boy, used in an informal and friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 对男子或男孩的非正式、友善的称呼
senses.example: He is a decent chap.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个正派的小伙子。
senses.why: The word began as a shortening of chapman, a trader, and then slid from merchant to any fellow.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是 chapman（商人）的缩略，随后从商人滑向任何男子。

senses.title: A crack in the skin
senses.definition: a painful split in the skin, especially on the hands or lips
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上疼痛的裂口，尤见于手部或嘴唇
senses.example: The cold wind left chaps on his hands.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风在他手上留下了裂口。
senses.why: A separate old verb meaning to split open gave this sense, which happens to share the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 另一个意为裂开的古动词给出了这个义项，恰好共用同一拼写。

senses.title: To crack from cold
senses.definition: to become rough and split because of cold or dry air
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷或干燥而变得粗糙开裂
senses.example: My lips chap in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 我的嘴唇冬天会皲裂。
senses.why: The splitting verb stayed in use for skin, so the noun and the verb keep one shape.
senses.whyCN: 表示裂开的动词一直用于皮肤，于是名词与动词保持同一形态。

intro.en: Chap has two histories: a shortening of chapman the trader, and an old verb meaning to split.
intro.cn: chap 有两段历史：一是商人 chapman 的缩略，二是意为裂开的古动词。

items.en: Ceapman meant a merchant or trader.
items.cn: 古英语 ceapman 意为商人或买卖人。

items.en: Chap shortened chapman and came to mean any man.
items.cn: chap 缩短了 chapman，转而指任何男子。

items.en: A separate verb chappen meant to crack open.
items.cn: 另一个动词 chappen 意为裂开。

items.en: Chapped skin kept the crack sense in daily use.
items.cn: 皲裂的皮肤让「裂开」义留在了日常用法里。

items.en: The friendly fellow sense and the skin sense now live side by side.
items.cn: 友善的男子义与皮肤裂口义如今并存。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trader root, while the meaning group lists words for a man.
note.cn: 形近组共享商人词根，近义组列出指男子的词。

entries.definition: an old word for a travelling seller
costing little money
rough and split by cold
a man, used informally
an informal word for a man
a British word for a man
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中指男子的词

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the trader root, the friendly phrase old chap and the skin sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用商人词根、友好说法 old chap 以及皮肤义。

normal.en: Chap was once chapman, the trader who walked from town to town.
normal.cn: chap 原本是 chapman，即走村串镇的商人。

normal.en: Old chap is the phrase that shows the word is warm rather than formal.
normal.cn: old chap 这个说法表明该词温暖而非正式。

normal.en: Chapped lips repeat the crack sense in a phrase you can see.
normal.cn: chapped lips 把「裂开」义放进一个看得见的搭配里。

normal.en: The plural chaps is both several men and several cracks.
normal.cn: 复数 chaps 既指几个男子，也指几道裂口。

normal.en: Remember cheap shares the trader root, since bargaining and selling belong together.
normal.cn: 记住 cheap 共享商人词根，因为讨价与买卖本是一体。

abstract.en: Picture a friendly stranger tipping his hat at a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个友善的陌生人在门口抬帽致意。

abstract.en: Picture red cracked knuckles after a day in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象吹了一天风后发红开裂的指节。

abstract.en: Picture a pedlar with a heavy pack on a country road.
abstract.cn: 想象乡间小路上背着沉重货包的小贩。

examples.en: The chap at the desk helped me at once.
examples.cn: 柜台后的那个小伙子马上帮了我。

examples.en: He is a funny old chap.
examples.cn: 他是个有趣的老家伙。

examples.en: Her hands chapped badly in the dry air.
examples.cn: 干燥的空气让她的手严重皲裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: chap 与 cheap 同源：小贩 chapman 讨价还价，后来 chap 就指街上随便一个家伙。

root: 表示「男子」的 chap 是 chapman（古英语 ceapman，商人）的缩略，与 cheap 同源；表示「皲裂」的 chap 来自中古英语 chappen（裂开），两词同形异源。

sensesIntro.en: A trader shortened into any fellow gives the friendly sense, while a splitting verb gives the skin sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 商人一词缩略为任何男子，给出友善义；裂开的动词则给出皮肤义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cheerful fellow met by chance on the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：在路上偶遇的一个快活家伙。

branches.en: A decent chap is a friendly judgement about a man.
branches.cn: a decent chap 是对一个男子的友善评价。

branches.en: A chap on the hand is a painful split.
branches.cn: 手上的 chap 是一道疼痛的裂口。

branches.en: The verb describes lips splitting in cold air.
branches.cn: 动词描述嘴唇在冷空气中裂开。

branches.en: One spelling carries two unrelated histories.
branches.cn: 一个拼写承载两段不相干的历史。

branches.en: The noun and verb of cracking share one shape.
branches.cn: 裂开的名词与动词共用一个形态。

intro.en: Chap keeps the trader root in chapman and the splitting root in chapped.
intro.cn: chap 在 chapman 中保留商人词根，在 chapped 中保留裂开词根。

latinIntro.en: The trader sense goes back to Old English ceap, a bargain, the same root as cheap.
latinIntro.cn: 商人义可追溯到古英语 ceap（交易），与 cheap 同根。

items.example: Ceap is the old trade word.

items.meaning: an informal word for a man

definition_zh: 挤；捏；榨；挤出；挤压；压榨；紧紧拥抱；挤过
definition_en: to press something firmly from opposite sides, or to get something out or through by pressing
core_image: 两只手掌从两侧用力向内合拢——汁水被榨出，身体从缝隙钻过
scene: 清晨的厨房里，橙子被切成了两半。 She gave the orange half a hard squeeze and juice ran into the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 squeeze 是「挤、榨」（第 1 个义项：用力挤压取汁）；句意为她用力一挤半个橙子，果汁流进了杯子。

pos.zh: 名词：挤压；榨取；紧握；拮据

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「榨汁器；挤压工具」
由本词加-ing 构成，义为「挤压（动作）」
由本词构成的俚语短语，义为「头号人物；要紧之人」

senses.title: To press something firmly from two sides
senses.definition: to press something hard from opposite sides, often to get liquid out
senses.definitionCN: 从相对两侧用力压某物，常为挤出汁液
senses.example: She squeezed the lemon over the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她把柠檬挤在鱼上。
senses.why: Two forces meet on one object; what is inside is pushed out.
senses.whyCN: 两股力在同一物体上相遇，内部的东西被推出来。

senses.title: To get through a narrow space
senses.definition: to manage to pass through a narrow or crowded space
senses.definitionCN: 设法通过狭窄或拥挤的空间
senses.example: He squeezed through the gap in the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他从篱笆的缺口挤了过去。
senses.why: Narrow walls press the body from both sides, like hands on fruit.
senses.whyCN: 狭窄的两壁从两侧挤压身体，如手掌挤压果子。

senses.title: To force something out of a place or position
senses.definition: to force something or someone out of a position or market by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用压力把某物或某人挤出某位置或市场
senses.example: Big stores squeezed out the small shops nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 大商店把附近的小店排挤了出去。
senses.why: Pressure from one side pushes the other side out of its place.
senses.whyCN: 一侧施压把另一侧挤出原有的位置。

senses.title: To press someone gently to show affection
senses.definition: to press a hand or arm lightly as a sign of warmth or support
senses.definitionCN: 轻握或轻捏他人的手、臂以表达温情或支持
senses.example: She gave his hand a gentle squeeze.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻捏了捏他的手。
senses.why: The same two-sided pressure, softened into a message of care.
senses.whyCN: 同样的双侧压力，被柔化成关怀的讯息。

senses.title: To manage to fit into time or space
senses.definition: to find room for something in a full schedule or space
senses.definitionCN: 在排满的时间表或空间里为某物腾出位置
senses.example: Can you squeeze in one more meeting today?
senses.exampleCN: 今天还能再安排一个会吗？
senses.why: A full schedule presses back; only force makes room.
senses.whyCN: 排满的日程如两壁相夹，须用力才腾出空隙。

senses.title: To press hard for money or advantage
senses.definition: to put pressure on someone to get money or unfair advantage
senses.definitionCN: 对某人施压以获取钱财或不正当好处
senses.example: The landlord squeezed every last coin from his tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 房东从租客身上榨取最后一枚硬币。
senses.why: People under pressure yield value, like fruit under the hand.
senses.whyCN: 受压的人会交出价值，如被手握住的果子。

senses.title: A difficult situation caused by lack
senses.definition: a period when money or supplies are hard to get
senses.definitionCN: 钱财或物资紧缺的时期
senses.example: Rising costs put a real squeeze on family budgets.
senses.exampleCN: 物价上涨让家庭预算颇为吃紧。
senses.why: Outside forces press in on the budget from both sides.
senses.whyCN: 外部力量从两侧挤压预算。

senses.title: The act or grip of squeezing
senses.definition: a single act of pressing, or the grip made by squeezing
senses.definitionCN: 一次按压的动作，或挤压形成的握力
senses.example: One firm squeeze of the trigger fired the shot.
senses.exampleCN: 用力一扣扳机，枪就响了。
senses.why: The action itself becomes a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 动作本身成为可数名词。

intro.en: Squeeze is an odd word: it appeared in English suddenly and its deeper origin is uncertain, though its meaning of pressing has never changed.
intro.cn: squeeze 来历特殊：它在英语中突然出现，更早的词源不确定，但「挤压」的含义从未改变。

items.en: No certain older root has been traced; some suggest a dialect or imitative source, all marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 尚未找到确切的上古词根；有方言起源或拟声起源之说，均属来源不确定。

items.en: The verb squeeze appears in English texts of the early 17th century, meaning to press hard.
items.cn: 动词 squeeze 于十七世纪初见诸英语文本，意为用力按压。

items.en: Old English cwysan "to crush" and related dialect words are cited as possible cousins, but the connection is not proven.
items.cn: 有人举出古英语 cwysan「压碎」及方言词为可能的亲属，但关联未获证实。

items.en: The noun sense of pressure and extortion developed in trade and social writing.
items.cn: 名词的「压力」「勒索」义在商业与社会文字中发展。

items.en: Modern use extends to budget squeezes, market squeezes, and affectionate squeezes.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖预算紧缩、市场挤压与亲昵的轻捏。

note.en: Squeeze shares one meaning-field with press-words and one shape-field with squ- words.
note.cn: squeeze 与按压类词共享一个义场，又与 squ- 词共享音形。

entries.definition: to blow air out suddenly through the nose
entries.definitionCN: 打喷嚏；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a short light sleep
entries.definitionCN: 小睡；打盹；拼写相近但词源不同

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks to hold squeeze in mind.

abstract.en: See yourself turning sideways to pass a narrow gate.

abstract.en: Picture a calendar so full that only force makes room.

sensesIntro.cn: squeeze 贯穿一个意象：两股力向内合拢——为取汁、为过隙、为亲昵、为钱财。

definition_zh: 察觉；感知；注意到；认为；视为；领会
definition_en: to become aware of something through the senses or the mind, or to regard something in a particular way
core_image: 一张网彻底罩住外界送来的信息，把它整个抓住
scene: 盲人用手杖轻敲地面。 The tip of the cane touched a raised edge before anyone could see it, and he could perceive the step under his feet.
sceneCN: 这里 perceive 是「凭感官察觉」（第 1 个义项：用感官接住它）；句意：手杖的尖端在任何人都还没看见之前就碰到了凸起的边缘，他凭触觉察觉到了脚下的台阶。图中可辨识物件：白色手杖、台阶边缘、导盲犬、行人、地面纹理；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有洞察力的；感知敏锐的

senses.title: Catch it through the senses
senses.definition: to become aware of something through sight, hearing, smell, touch, or taste
senses.definitionCN: 通过视觉、听觉、嗅觉、触觉或味觉意识到某物
senses.example: She perceived a faint smell of smoke in the hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 她察觉到走廊里有一丝烟味。
senses.why: Latin percipere joins per- 'thoroughly' to capere 'to take'. Perception is a taking hold: the senses reach out and grasp what the world offers, which is why the word works for every sense at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 percipere 把 per-“彻底”与 capere“拿取”结合。感知就是抓住：感官伸出去，把外界送来的东西握在手里，因此这个词能同时用于所有感官。

senses.title: Notice a small change
senses.definition: to notice something subtle that might easily be missed
senses.definitionCN: 注意到容易被忽略的细微之处
senses.example: The doctor perceived a slight change in his breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生察觉到他呼吸的细微变化。
senses.why: The 'thorough' in per- explains why the word often implies effort: the change is small, and the observer has to take hold of it before it disappears.
senses.whyCN: per- 里的“彻底”解释了为什么这个词常隐含用力：变化很小，观察者必须在它消失之前把它抓住。

senses.title: Realize: come to know
senses.definition: to come to realize or understand a fact, often gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐意识到或明白一个事实
senses.example: I perceived that the plan would not work.
senses.exampleCN: 我意识到这个计划行不通。
senses.why: Mental grasp uses the same hand as physical grasp. Once the mind closes on a fact, the fact is held, and English lets perceive cover that inner taking as well.
senses.whyCN: 心智的把握与身体的抓取用同一只手。一旦心思合拢在一个事实上，这个事实就被握住了，英语也让 perceive 覆盖这种内在的拿取。

senses.title: Regard it as: perceive as
senses.definition: to regard or classify something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定方式看待或归类某事物
senses.example: Many voters perceive the tax as unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 许多选民认为这项税不公平。
senses.why: What you take hold of is not only the object but the category you put it in. The construction perceive as marks that act of placing, which is why it dominates in opinion research.
senses.whyCN: 你抓住的不只是对象，还包括你把它放进的那个类别。perceive as 这一结构标记“归类放置”的动作，因此它在民意研究中占主导。

senses.title: Grasp a meaning
senses.definition: to understand the meaning or significance of something said, written, or shown
senses.definitionCN: 理解所说、所写或所展示之物的含义或意义
senses.example: He perceived the irony in her remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他领会了她话里的讽刺。
senses.why: Meaning is not visible on the surface of words. To perceive it is to take hold of something that is implied rather than displayed, and this sense has been central since the Latin verb also meant 'to understand'.
senses.whyCN: 意义并不写在词语表面。领会它就是抓住某种被暗示而非被展示的东西；自拉丁语动词兼有“理解”义以来，这一义项一直是核心。

senses.title: Be seen in a certain light
senses.definition: in the passive, to be viewed or judged in a particular way by others
senses.definitionCN: 被动式中，被他人以特定方式看待或评判
senses.example: The reform is widely perceived as a retreat.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革被普遍视为一种退却。
senses.why: Perception is not only what an individual grasps but what a public settles on. In the passive the word names a shared judgement, which is why it appears so often in political and media language.
senses.whyCN: 感知不只是个人抓住什么，也包括公众最终认定什么。被动式中，这个词命名的是一种共同判断，因此它频繁出现在政治与媒体语言里。

senses.title: Perception as a field of study
senses.definition: in psychology, the process by which sensory input is detected, organized, and given meaning
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，感官输入被检测、组织并赋予意义的过程
senses.example: The study tests how colour perception changes with age.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验颜色知觉如何随年龄变化。
senses.why: Psychology separates the raw signal from the interpreted result. The word then names the whole pipeline from sensation to meaning, and perception becomes a countable object of experiment.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把原始信号与解释后的结果分开。这个词于是命名从感觉到意义的整条流水线，perception 也变成实验中可计数的对象。

senses.title: Perceive without senses: grasp by intuition
senses.titleCN: 不靠感官的领会：直觉把握
senses.definition: in older or religious usage, to apprehend a truth directly, without sensory evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老或宗教的用法中，不经感官证据而直接把握一个真理
senses.example: The mystics claimed to perceive a unity behind all things.
senses.exampleCN: 神秘主义者声称领悟到万物背后的统一。
senses.why: If perception is a taking hold, it does not have to happen through the body. Religious and philosophical writers extended it to the mind's direct grasp of truths, keeping the hand and dropping the senses.
senses.whyCN: 如果感知就是抓住，那么它不必通过身体发生。宗教与哲学作者把它扩展到心智对真理的直接把握：保留那只手，放下感官。

intro.en: Perceive is Latin in origin and replaced an Old English verb. Its root is capere 'to take', not the cent- of percentage: the shared per- is a prefix, not a common root.
intro.cn: perceive 源自拉丁语，取代了一个古英语动词。它的词根是 capere“拿取”，而不是 percentage 的 cent-：两者共有的 per- 只是前缀，不是共同词根。

items.en: Perceive is recorded, from the Anglo-French stem parceif-, from Old French perçoivre, from Latin percipere.
items.cn: perceive 记录于 1300 年前后，来自盎格鲁-法语词干 parceif-，再上溯古法语 perçoivre 与拉丁语 percipere。

items.en: Percipere means 'to obtain, grasp, understand'. It joins per- 'thoroughly' to capere 'to take, seize'. The image is a complete taking hold, not a passing look.
items.cn: percipere 意为“获得、抓住、理解”。它把 per-“彻底”与 capere“拿取、抓住”结合。画面是“彻底握住”，而不是“瞥一眼”。

items.en: Capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp', the source also of capture, accept, and capable. The asterisk marks a reconstructed root.
items.cn: capere 上溯原始印欧语 *kap-“抓取”，也是 capture、accept、capable 的来源。星号表示重构词根。

items.en: Perceive displaces the Old English verbs ongietan 'to grasp, understand' and gefredan 'to feel'. The newcomers from French took over the mental as well as the sensory field.
items.cn: perceive 取代古英语动词 ongietan“抓住、理解”与 gefredan“感觉”。这些来自法语的新词同时接管了心智与感官两个领域。

items.en: The noun perception is fixed in philosophy, then in psychology, where it names the processing of sensory input. The passive 'is perceived as' becomes standard in public opinion language.
items.cn: 名词 perception 先在哲学中定型，后在心理学中命名感官输入的处理过程。被动式“is perceived as”成为民意语言的标准说法。

note.en: The first group is per- words with different roots; the second compares verbs of noticing and judging.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 per-、但词根不同的词；第二组比较表示“注意与判断”的动词。

entries.definition: to keep something safe or unchanged. It looks close but its root is servare 'to keep', not capere.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某物、使其不变。外形相近，但词根是 servare“保存”，不是 capere。

entries.definition: deliberately turning away from what is right or reasonable. Its root is vertere 'to turn', so it is a turning aside, not a grasping.
entries.definitionCN: 故意背离正确或合理之事。其词根是 vertere“转”，因此是“转开”，不是“抓住”。

entries.definition: to keep going despite difficulty. Its root is severus 'strict, serious', a different family from capere.
entries.definitionCN: 遇到困难仍坚持下去。其词根是 severus“严格、严肃”，与 capere 属不同词族。

entries.definition: able to be noticed. It is built on the same perception stem, so it is a true relative, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: 能被察觉的。它建立在同一个 perception 词干上，是真正的同族词，而不是形近词。

entries.definition: to become aware of something by paying attention. It is more casual and often momentary; perceive can imply a fuller grasp.
entries.definitionCN: 通过注意而意识到某物。它更随意、常为瞬间；perceive 可暗示更完整的把握。

entries.definition: to become aware of something without being able to say exactly why. It stresses intuition; perceive can be sensory or reasoned.
entries.definitionCN: 说不出确切理由地意识到某事。它强调直觉；perceive 可以是感官的，也可以是推理的。

entries.definition: to look on or consider in a particular way. It matches the 'perceive as' sense but lacks the sensory meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式看待或考虑。它对应“perceive as”这一义项，但没有感官义。

entries.definition: to see or understand something that is not obvious, especially a difference. It stresses discrimination, while perceive stresses awareness.
entries.definitionCN: 看出或理解不明显之物，尤指差别。它强调分辨，而 perceive 强调觉察。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on per- and taking, then three abstract images about grasping what is not obvious.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 per- 与“拿取”的挂钩，再用三个关于“抓住不明显之物”的抽象画面。

normal.en: per- means thoroughly, -ceive comes from capere 'take'. To perceive is to take something in completely.
normal.cn: per- 是“彻底”，-ceive 来自 capere“拿取”。perceive 就是把某物完整地拿进来。

normal.en: receive, deceive, perceive all hide capere: each is a different way of taking.
normal.cn: receive、deceive、perceive 都藏着 capere：每一种都是不同方式的“拿”。

normal.en: perceive as: the 'as' is the box you put the thing into. You take it and file it under a label.
normal.cn: perceive as：那个 as 就是你把它放进去的盒子。你抓住它，再贴上一个标签归档。

normal.en: A blind person's cane perceives the step before the eyes do: the hand takes hold first.
normal.cn: 盲人的手杖先于眼睛感知到台阶：手先抓住。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with percent: perceive has a c-e-i-v-e root of taking, while percent counts hundreds.
normal.cn: 别和 percent 混：perceive 的 c-e-i-v-e 是“拿取”词根，percent 数的是“百”。

abstract.en: Perception is never passive: to perceive is to select, and selection is already interpretation.
abstract.cn: 感知从不被动：感知就是选择，而选择已经是解释。

abstract.en: What a group perceives becomes real in its consequences, even if the perception is wrong.
abstract.cn: 一个群体所感知的东西会通过后果变成现实，即使这个感知是错的。

abstract.en: To perceive a meaning is to take hold of something no one can hand you.
abstract.cn: 领会一层含义，就是抓住一件没有人能直接交给你的东西。

examples.en: The sensor perceives motion and turns on the light.
examples.cn: 传感器感知到动作，随即打开灯。

examples.en: Tourists often perceive the city as safer than residents do.
examples.cn: 游客常常比本地居民更觉得这座城市安全。

examples.en: It took her a moment to perceive why the room had gone quiet.
examples.cn: 她花了一会儿才领会房间为何安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.note: per- 记成“彻底”，-ceive 记成“拿”（capere）：把外界的东西整个拿进来，就是感知。
dict_mnemonic.text: per（彻底）+ ceive（拿取）→ 彻底抓住 → 察觉、感知、领会、视为

root: 拉丁 percipere“抓住、领会”＝per（彻底）+ capere（拿取，原始印欧语 *kap-）→ 古法语 perçoivre → 英语 perceive。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from the senses themselves to subtle noticing, to realizing, to the category you put a thing in, to grasping meaning, to being seen by a public, to the science of perception, and finally to a grasp that needs no senses at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从感官本身开始，转到细微察觉、意识到、把事物放进某个类别、领会含义、被公众看待、作为研究对象的知觉，最后落到完全不需要感官的把握。

core.en: A hand closing completely around what the world holds out
core.cn: 一只手彻底合拢，握住外界递来的东西

branches.en: Sensory grasp: what the body detects, and how psychology models that detection.
branches.cn: 感官把握：身体检测到什么，以及心理学如何建模这一检测。

branches.en: Small signal to inner fact: noticing a change, then realizing what it means.
branches.cn: 从小信号到内在事实：察觉变化，然后意识到它意味着什么。

branches.en: Being placed: in the passive, someone is seen in a certain light.
branches.cn: 被放置：被动式中，某人被以某种眼光看待。

branches.en: Meaning without a surface: reading irony, and grasping a truth without senses.
branches.cn: 没有表面的意义：读出讽刺，以及不靠感官把握真理。

branches.en: The label: the same grasp that takes the thing files it under a category.
branches.cn: 标签：抓住事物的同一动作，也把它归入某个类别。

intro.en: Perceive's family centres on the -ceive / -cept stem from capere: perception, perceptive, perceptible, and the modern misperceive.
intro.cn: perceive 的词族以 capere 而来的 -ceive / -cept 词干为中心：perception、perceptive、perceptible，以及现代的 misperceive。

latinIntro.en: Latin percipere and its noun perceptio are the direct sources. Capere 'to take' supplies the stem; per- adds the idea of thoroughness, not a separate root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 percipere 及其名词 perceptio 是直接来源。capere“拿取”提供词干；per- 增加“彻底”之意，并不是另一个词根。

items.meaning: to become aware of, grasp, or regard
items.example: We perceived a change in the tone.

items.meaning: awareness; the process of perceiving; a view

items.meaningCN: 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
items.example: A perceptive reader spots the hint.
items.exampleCN: 敏锐的读者会看出那个暗示。
有一段能察觉到的停顿。

items.meaning: in a way that can be noticed

items.example: People misperceive the risk of rare events.
items.exampleCN: 人们会错估罕见事件的风险。

items.example: The perceiver's position shapes the report.
items.exampleCN: 感知者的位置塑造了这份报告。

items.example: Capere is the root of capture and accept.
items.exampleCN: capere 是 capture 与 accept 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Percipere is the direct source of perceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: percipere 是 perceive 的直接来源。
perceptio 是英语 perception 的基础。
capere 提供 perceive 中的 -ceive。

latinEntries.example: Perceptivus is the base of English perceptive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: perceptivus 是英语 perceptive 的基础。

definition_en: a unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram, or a kind of chickpea
core_image: 天平上的小砝码标着克数，旁边放着一小撮白色的糖
scene: 这枚硬币大约重五克。 The coin weighs about five grams.
sceneCN: 这里 gram 是「克」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这枚硬币大约重五克。

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a metric unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram
senses.definitionCN: 公制重量单位，等于千分之一千克
senses.example: The coin weighs about five grams.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚硬币大约重五克。
senses.why: This is the scientific and everyday unit sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是科学与日常使用的单位含义。

senses.title: A kind of pea
senses.definition: a small yellow split pea used in South Asian cooking
senses.definitionCN: 南亚烹饪中使用的小粒黄色豆
senses.example: Gram flour is used in Indian cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 鹰嘴豆粉用于印度菜。
senses.why: The plant word came through Portuguese from an older Indian name.
senses.whyCN: 这个植物词经葡萄牙语来自更古老的印度名称。

intro.en: Gram was coined in France from a Greek word for a small weight.
intro.cn: gram 由法国人根据希腊语中表示小重量的词创造。

items.en: Gramma meant a small weight and a written mark.
items.cn: gramma 意为小重量和书写的记号。

items.en: Gramme was coined for the new metric unit.
items.cn: gramme 被创造出来表示新的公制单位。

items.en: Gram entered English with the metric system.
items.cn: gram 随公制进入英语。

items.en: It became a building block of kilogram and milligram.

scene: 洗手间的水声停了，门开了。 The sign pointed to the toilets downstairs.

senses.title: The bowl and its fittings
senses.definition: a fixed bowl with a seat and flush, used for getting rid of body waste
senses.definitionCN: 带座圈与冲水装置的固定洁具，用于排走身体废物
senses.example: The toilet will not flush properly.
senses.exampleCN: 马桶冲水不畅。
senses.why: The core image is a small room that washes waste away.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把污物冲走的小房间。

senses.title: The room containing the bowl
senses.definition: a room with a toilet and often a washbasin
senses.definitionCN: 设有马桶（常含洗手池）的房间
senses.example: Where are the toilets in this station?
senses.exampleCN: 这个车站的厕所在哪儿？
senses.why: The fixture names the room that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 洁具命名了容纳它的房间。

senses.title: The act of washing and dressing
senses.definition: the process of washing, grooming and dressing, especially one's toilet
senses.definitionCN: 洗漱、打理与穿衣的过程，尤指 one's toilet
senses.example: She spent an hour at her toilet before the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 舞会前她花了一个小时梳妆。
senses.why: The older sense: a cloth for grooming became the grooming itself.
senses.whyCN: 旧义：一块梳妆布演变为梳妆本身。

senses.title: Grooming articles
senses.definition: articles used in washing and grooming, as in toiletries
senses.definitionCN: 用于洗漱打理的物品，如 toiletries

senses.exampleCN: 把梳洗用品装进小包。
senses.why: The grooming act extends to its tools.
senses.whyCN: 梳妆行为延伸到它的工具。

senses.title: A cleansing or rinse of a wound
senses.definition: in medical use, the cleansing of a wound or body part

senses.example: The nurse carried out the toilet of the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 护士为伤口做了清洁处理。
senses.why: Grooming turns inward, cleaning what is hurt.

definition_en: a fixed set of steps that must be followed to carry out a task, a formal process or a medical treatment
core_image: 手术室外的走廊上，一张写满步骤的卡片贴在墙上，医生拿笔逐项打勾
scene: 手术开始前，主刀医生和护士对着墙上的步骤卡逐项核对了一遍。 The team followed the written procedure step by step before the operation began.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「为完成某事而必须依次执行的一套步骤」（第 1 个义项：固定顺序的操作步骤）；句意为手术开始前，团队按书面步骤逐项执行。图中可辨识物件：步骤卡、打勾用的笔、手术室门、走廊指示灯；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 进行中的事项；诉讼程序

senses.title: A fixed series of steps
senses.definition: an ordered set of actions that must be followed to complete a task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项任务而必须依次执行的一组动作
senses.example: The lab has a written procedure for handling every sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室对每一个样本的处理都有书面步骤。
senses.why: The word came from a verb meaning to go forward, so a procedure is a path laid out to be walked in order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自意为「向前走」的动词，因此程序就是一条铺好、须按顺序走完的路线。

senses.title: The official way of handling a matter
senses.definition: the recognized sequence by which an official body accepts, hears or decides something
senses.definitionCN: 官方机构受理、审议或决定某事所认可的次序
senses.example: The complaint went through the standard procedure for appeals.
senses.exampleCN: 这项投诉走了标准的上诉手续。
senses.why: Anything a body must do in a set order becomes a procedure, because the order is what makes the decision valid.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须按固定次序完成的事都叫程序，因为正是这个次序使决定有效。

senses.title: A medical treatment that acts on the body
senses.definition: a treatment in which a doctor performs a defined action on or inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 医生在体表或体内施行的一套明确操作
senses.example: The procedure took forty minutes and needed no overnight stay.
senses.exampleCN: 这台操作用了四十分钟，不需要留院过夜。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for any defined course of action on a patient, and the sense narrowed to interventions.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词指对病人的一套明确处置，后来收窄为各种介入操作。

senses.title: The accepted order of business in a meeting
senses.definition: the rules that govern how a meeting or assembly conducts its business
senses.definitionCN: 会议或议会处理事务时遵循的规则
senses.example: The chair reminded the committee of its own procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 主席提醒委员会注意自己定的议事规程。
senses.why: A meeting is valid only if it moves through the agreed steps, so the rules of order took this name.
senses.whyCN: 会议只有按商定的步骤推进才有效，因此议事规则也用了这个名称。

senses.title: A named block of code in a program
senses.definition: a section of a program that performs one task and returns control to the point that called it
senses.definitionCN: 程序中完成单项任务并把控制权交回调用处的一段代码
senses.example: The program calls the same procedure every time it reads a record.
senses.exampleCN: 程序每读一条记录就调用同一个子程序。
senses.why: Computing reused the word for a routine because a routine is a small ordered path through the machine's work.
senses.whyCN: 计算机把这个词用于例行程序，因为一段例程就是机器工作中一条小型有序路径。

senses.title: The usual way a job is done in a place
senses.definition: the established way of doing a job in a particular workplace, whether or not it is written down
senses.definitionCN: 某一工作场所既定的做事方式，无论是否写成文字
senses.example: Checking the seals twice is procedure on this rig, not a personal habit.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座钻井平台上，密封件查两遍是规程，不是个人习惯。
senses.why: An unwritten habit becomes procedure once a crew treats it as the required order, so the word covers custom as well as rule.
senses.whyCN: 一旦班组把它当作必须遵循的次序，未成文的习惯也成了程序，因此这个词兼指惯例与规章。

senses.title: The steps by which a case moves through court
senses.definition: the rules that fix what a party must file, when and in what form during litigation
senses.definitionCN: 规定当事人在诉讼中须提交什么、何时提交、以何种形式提交的规则
senses.example: Civil procedure decides what a plaintiff must file and when.
senses.exampleCN: 民事诉讼程序决定原告必须提交什么、何时提交。
senses.why: Legal systems separate substance from steps, and the steps are called procedure because they carry a case forward in order.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系把实体与步骤分开，而这些步骤被称为程序，因为它们按次序把一个案子往前推进。

senses.title: One stage in an industrial process
senses.titleCN: 工序；工艺流程中的一环
senses.definition: a single defined operation within a manufacturing or chemical sequence
senses.definitionCN: 制造或化工流程中一道界限明确的加工步骤
senses.example: Each procedure in the line has its own temperature range.
senses.exampleCN: 流水线上每一道工序都有自己的温度区间。
senses.why: A factory breaks a long making into ordered steps, and each step inherits the name of the whole path.
senses.whyCN: 工厂把漫长的制造拆成有序步骤，每一道步骤都继承了整条路径的名称。

intro.en: Procedure came through French from Latin procedere 'to go forward', built on pro- 'forward' and cedere 'to go, to yield'. The pre-Latin root of cedere is a reconstruction. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语「向前走」的动词，由意为「向前」的前缀与意为「走、让」的动词构成。后者更早的词根属重构形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to withdraw, to yield'. Its deeper origin is not attested; the root usually proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、退、让」。其更深来源没有书证；通常为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus cedere produced procedere 'to go forward, to advance, to continue'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 cedere 构成 procedere，意为「向前走、推进、继续」。

items.en: Late and Medieval Latin formed procedura for the manner of proceeding in a matter, especially in law.
items.cn: 晚期与中世纪拉丁语构成 procedura，指处理某事的进行方式，尤用于法律。

items.en: French procédure brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as the conduct of a legal action.
items.cn: 法语 procédure 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指法律诉讼的进行方式。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word covered meeting rules, from the nineteenth medical interventions, and from the twentieth a block of code in computing.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个词涵盖议事规则；十九世纪起涵盖医疗介入；二十世纪起涵盖计算机中的代码段。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin verb of going, plus one word of Greek origin that looks similar; group two holds words for ways of doing things.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「走」动词的词，外加一个形似而来源不同的希腊词；第二组是表示做事方式的近义词。

entries.definition: A continuous course of change rather than an ordered checklist; the same Latin verb, a different noun suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 指连续变化的过程，而非有序清单；同一拉丁动词，名词后缀不同。

entries.definition: The carrying on of an action, or its record in court; it names the activity, not the rules for it.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的进行，或其在法庭上的记录；它指活动本身，而不是活动的规则。

entries.definition: Pra- 'before' plus cedere: something that went before and now guides later decisions, not a set of steps.
entries.definitionCN: pra-「在前」加 cedere：先前发生、如今指导后续决定的事例，不是一套步骤。

entries.definition: From Greek protokollon, the first sheet glued to a roll; it became a diplomatic or technical code, not a Latin path.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语「贴在卷首的第一张纸」，后来指外交或技术约定，与拉丁的「路径」无关。

entries.definition: A systematic way of doing something, often chosen by the doer rather than imposed by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性的做法，常由执行者自行选择，而非由权威规定。

entries.definition: A regular way of doing something because it is familiar and repeated, with no claim of formal validity.
entries.definitionCN: 因熟悉而重复的惯常做法，并不强调正式效力。

entries.definition: A single action in a sequence; a procedure is the whole sequence of such actions.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的单个动作；程序则是这些动作的整个序列。

entries.definition: The organized set of parts and rules taken together, wider than one procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 由各部分与规则构成的整体安排，比单个程序更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: 'Forward' plus 'to go': a procedure is a path laid out so that work can be walked through in order.
normal.cn: 「向前」加「走」：程序就是一条铺好的路径，让工作按顺序走完。

normal.en: The same verb yields the verb to continue, the noun for a court record and the word for a continuous process.
normal.cn: 同一动词还给出表示「继续」的动词、表示法庭记录的名词，以及表示连续过程的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: standard procedure, safety procedure, legal procedure, surgical procedure.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：标准程序、安全规程、法律程序、外科手术。

normal.en: A hospital, a court and a committee each keep a written path that must be followed in order.
normal.cn: 医院、法院与委员会各自都有一份必须按顺序走完的书面路径。

normal.en: Computing calls a small ordered routine a procedure because it is a short path through the machine's work.
normal.cn: 计算机把一小段有序例程称为子程序，因为它是机器工作中一条短路径。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor with numbered doors, each of which must be opened before the next one.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每隔一段有一扇编号的门，必须依次打开。

abstract.en: Picture a dance notation that only works if every count is danced in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一份舞谱，只有每一拍都踩准才成立。

abstract.en: Picture a legal file that is valid only because every stamp sits in the right order.
abstract.cn: 想象一份法律卷宗，只因每枚印章次序正确才有效。

examples.en: Changing the procedure required the approval of the whole committee.
examples.cn: 更改程序需要全体委员会批准。

examples.en: The surgeon explained the procedure to the family in plain words.
examples.cn: 外科医生用平实的话向家属解释了这台手术。

examples.en: A missing signature sent the file back to the start of the procedure.
examples.cn: 少了一个签名，文件被退回程序的起点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ ced（走）+ ure（名词）」——一路向前走完的路线 → 程序、步骤、手续

root: 拉丁语「向前走」的动词由意为「向前」的前缀与意为「走、让」的动词构成，加名词后缀再构成「进行方式」；该动词更早的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one path: a set of steps is laid down, then adopted by an office, applied to a body, imposed on a meeting, coded into a machine, hardened into local custom, stretched into litigation and finally shortened to one stage on a factory line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条路径展开：先铺下一套步骤，再被机构采用、施于身体、用于会议、写进机器，固化为本地惯例，延伸为诉讼，最后缩短为工厂流水线上的一环。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered card on the wall of a hospital corridor, each line ticked in order before anyone may proceed.
core.cn: 核心意象：医院走廊墙上一张编号卡片，每一行都按顺序打勾后才允许继续。

branches.en: LAID PATH AND LOCAL HABIT: a written sequence and an unwritten one are the same order once a crew treats it as required.
branches.cn: 铺好的路径与本地习惯：书面次序与未成文次序，一旦被班组视为必须，便是同一种次序。

branches.en: FORMAL VALIDITY: what an office accepts and what a court requires are both orders that make a result valid.
branches.cn: 正式效力：机构受理与法院要求，都是使结果有效的次序。

branches.en: ONE OPERATION: a treatment on a body and a stage on a line are single steps cut out of a longer path.
branches.cn: 单次操作：施于身体的一台操作与流水线上的一道工序，都是从更长路径中截出的单步。

branches.en: RULES OF ORDER: a meeting valid only if it moves through the agreed steps.
branches.cn: 议事规则：会议只有按商定步骤推进才有效。

branches.en: CODED PATH: computing writes the same ordered path into a block of instructions.
branches.cn: 编码路径：计算机把同一条有序路径写成一段指令。

intro.en: Procedure is a Latin noun of path and motion: a prefix meaning forward, a verb meaning to go, and a noun suffix marking the result.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示路径与运动的拉丁名词：一个意为「向前」的前缀、一个意为「走」的动词，以及标记结果的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere gives proceed, process, precede and succeed; pro- adds forward motion; the noun suffix marks a way of doing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「走」动词衍生出继续、过程、先于与接着等词；「向前」前缀加进向前的运动；名词后缀标记一种做法。

items.structure: cedere, cessi, cessum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root carries movement along a line.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载沿一条线移动的意思。

items.example: The prefix fixes the direction of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀确定运动的方向。

items.example: The verb is the whole path in one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用一个词表达了整条路径。

items.example: The noun turned the path into a thing that can be written down.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把路径变成可以写下来的东西。

items.example: The English noun still means a path to be walked.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词仍指一条要走完的路径。

items.meaning: result or instrument of an action
items.example: The suffix marks the outcome of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记动词的结果。

items.meaning: relating to steps or formal rules
items.meaningCN: 与步骤或正式规则有关的
items.example: A procedural objection concerns how a decision was made.
items.exampleCN: 程序性异议针对决定是怎么样作出的。

items.example: The train proceeded once the signal changed.
items.exampleCN: 信号一变，列车继续前行。

items.example: The same verb, seen as a flowing course rather than a checklist.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词，被看作流动的过程而非清单。

definition_en: relating to the home or family, to one's own country, or to animals kept by people
core_image: 厨房窗台上晾着洗好的碗，楼下传来自家孩子的脚步声
scene: 周末早晨厨房里飘着面包香，孩子还在客厅搭积木。 Domestic chores fall to her on Sundays.
sceneCN: 这里 domestic 是「家庭的、家务的」（第 1 个义项：与家庭和家务有关）；句意是星期天大部分家务都落在她身上。

pos.zh: 形容词：家庭的；家务的；国内的；驯养的
名词：家仆（旧用法，多用于英式英语）

senses.title: Of the home and household
senses.definition: relating to the home, the household or family life
senses.definitionCN: 与家、家庭生活或家务有关的
senses.example: They argued about how to share domestic work.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为如何分担家务争吵过。
senses.why: Latin domus meant house, so the adjective begins as a word about everything inside the walls of a home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 domus 是「房子」，所以这个形容词一开始就指家门以内的一切。

senses.title: Within one country
senses.definition: relating to one's own country rather than to foreign countries
senses.definitionCN: 与本国内部有关，而非与外国有关的
senses.example: Domestic flights leave from the older terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 国内航班从较旧的航站楼出发。
senses.why: A country is imagined as a large household, so affairs inside its borders are domestic affairs.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家被想象成一个大家庭，因此国境之内的事务就是「家里的」事务。

senses.title: Tamed, not wild
senses.definition: kept by people as a pet or farm animal rather than living in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养作宠物或农用，而非野生生活的
senses.example: The farm keeps both domestic and wild species.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场既养家养品种，也养野生物种。
senses.why: An animal brought into the house or the yard has crossed the same boundary as a household matter.
senses.whyCN: 被带进屋里或院里的动物，和家务事一样跨过了「家门」这条界线。

intro.en: Domestic comes from Latin domesticus, belonging to the house, and the root domus, house.
intro.cn: domestic 来自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），其根是 domus（房子）。

items.en: The root behind domus is generally reconstructed as a word for house or household; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: domus 背后的词根一般重构为表示「房子、家户」的形式，具体形态不确定。

items.en: Domus meant a house or a household, and it produced dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，它还生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domesticus meant belonging to the household, and it was also used for household servants.
items.cn: domesticus 表示「属于家户的」，也用来指家仆。

items.en: Old French domestique passed the adjective into English with both the home and the servant senses.
items.cn: 古法语 domestique 把这个形容词带入英语，家庭义与家仆义一并传入。

items.en: English extended the word from the household to the nation, speaking of domestic affairs.
items.cn: 英语把它从家户扩展到国家，开始说 domestic affairs（国内事务）。

items.en: The adjective now covers chores, flights, animals and products of a whole country.
items.cn: 今天这个形容词覆盖家务、航班、动物，以及一国的产品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin domus root; the near-meaning group gathers household and internal words.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 domus 词根；近义组收的是家庭与「内部」类的词。

entries.definition: To tame an animal or bring it into human use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驯化、使家养」，由本词加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: The quality or state of home life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家庭生活、恋家」，同出 domus。

entries.definition: A person's permanent home, from Latin domicilium; it shares domus but has a different spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所」，来自拉丁语 domicilium；与 domestic 同出 domus，但拼写路径不同。

entries.definition: All the people living together in one home; often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「家户、家庭的」，指同住一屋的人。

entries.definition: Inside a country or organisation; the usual word in political contexts for domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，在政治语境中常与 domestic 对应。

entries.definition: An animal that is no longer wild; narrower than domestic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「驯服的」，范围比 domestic 的驯养义更窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real domus family from the house to the nation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 domus 词族，从房子一直走到国家。

normal.en: Domus is house; domesticus is what belongs to the house.
normal.cn: domus 是房子，domesticus 就是属于这座房子的。

normal.en: Dominus, master of the house, comes from the same domus.
normal.cn: dominus 意为一家之主，也出自同一个 domus。

normal.en: A domestic flight stays inside the country, as if the nation were one house.
normal.cn: 国内航班留在国境之内，仿佛整个国家是一间大房子。

normal.en: Domestic animals have been brought into the human household.
normal.cn: 家养动物已经被带进了人类的家庭。

normal.en: Gross domestic product counts what is produced inside those borders.
normal.cn: 国内生产总值算的是这些边界之内生产的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a warm kitchen seen from the street, with one lamp still on.
abstract.cn: 想象从街上望见一间温暖的厨房，还亮着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Picture a map of one country drawn as a single house.
abstract.cn: 想象把一国的地图画成一间房子。

abstract.en: Picture a fence where wild grass stops and a swept yard begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，外面是野草，里面是扫干净的院子。

examples.en: Domestic work should not fall on one person alone.
examples.cn: 家务不应只落在一个人身上。

examples.en: The airline added two new domestic routes.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司新增了两条国内航线。

examples.en: Domestic cats sleep far more than their wild cousins.
examples.cn: 家猫比野外的同类睡得多得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: dom 有「家、屋」的意思，-estic 是形容词后缀：属于这间屋子的，就是家庭的、国内的。

root: 源自拉丁语 domesticus（属于家的），由 domus（房子、家户）加形容词后缀 -icus 构成；domus 同时生出 dominus（一家之主）。古法语 domestique 把家庭义与家仆义传入英语，十六世纪起从家户扩展指国家内部。

sensesIntro.en: One root imagines a house, then stretches it to a nation and to animals brought indoors.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根先想象一间房子，再把它拉到整个国家，以及被带进屋里的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kitchen seen from the street, warm inside and swept clean.
core.cn: 核心意象：从街上望见的一间厨房，里面温暖，地面扫得干净。

branches.en: THE HOME: the first sense covers everything inside the walls of a house.
branches.cn: 家庭线：第一个义项覆盖家门以内的一切。

branches.en: THE NATION: a country is treated as a large household, so inside affairs are domestic.
branches.cn: 国家线：国家被当作大家庭，因此境内事务称作 domestic。

branches.en: THE YARD: tame animals have crossed the same boundary into human keeping.
branches.cn: 院子线：驯养动物跨过同一条界线，进入人的照料范围。

branches.en: House and country share the word because both are spaces one belongs to.
branches.cn: 家庭与国家共用一个词，因为两者都是人所属的空间。

branches.en: A domestic animal is simply a creature moved into the household.
branches.cn: 家养动物不过是被移进家户的一种生物。

intro.en: Domestic joins the Latin house root domus to the adjective suffix -icus, which English keeps as -ic.
intro.cn: domestic 把拉丁语「房子」词根 domus 接到形容词后缀 -icus 上，英语保留为 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, domesticus and dominus are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、domesticus 与 dominus 均有记录，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

definition_en: a result of an action, or importance in a situation
core_image: 推倒第一张骨牌，后面的牌一张张跟着倒
scene: 他没带伞就出门，回来时浑身湿透。 Skipping breakfast had clear consequences for his day.
sceneCN: 这里 consequence 指「后果」（第 1 个义项：行为带来的结果）；句意是不吃早饭对他这一天造成了明显的后果。

derivatives.zh: 随之发生的；作为结果的

senses.title: A result
senses.definition: a result that follows from an action or condition
senses.definitionCN: 由行为或情况引发的直接结果
senses.example: The consequence of the delay was a lost contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误的后果是丢了一份合同。
senses.why: Every action sets a line in motion, and the line arrives somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 每个行动都让一条线开始运动，而这条线终会抵达某处。

senses.title: Importance
senses.definition: importance or significance, often in the phrase of consequence
senses.definitionCN: 重要性或意义，常见于 of consequence 的说法
senses.example: The decision was of great consequence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定关系重大。
senses.why: Something that pulls many other things behind it must be heavy.
senses.whyCN: 能拉动许多别的东西的事物，本身一定很重。

senses.title: A logical conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion drawn from a set of facts
senses.definitionCN: 由一组事实推出的结论
senses.example: From these facts one consequence is unavoidable.

intro.en: Consequence comes from Latin consequentia, a following after, from com-, together, and sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: consequence 来自拉丁语 consequentia，意为随后而来，由 com-（一起）与 sequi（跟随）构成。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow behind someone.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟在某人后面。

items.en: Consequi meant to follow after and reach the same point.
items.cn: consequi 意为随后跟到同一点。

items.en: Consequentia named what follows from something else.
items.cn: consequentia 指由别的事物引出的东西。

items.en: Old French consequence used the word for a result.
items.cn: 古法语 consequence 用这个词指结果。

items.en: English consequence first meant what follows in logic.
items.cn: 英语 consequence 最初指逻辑上随之而来的东西。

items.en: It now also means weight or importance.
items.cn: 如今它也指分量或重要性。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin follow base, and the meaning group names other results.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语跟随词基，近义组列出其他表示结果的词。

entries.definition: a set of things in a fixed order
entries.definitionCN: 按固定顺序排列的一系列事物

entries.definition: following as a result
as a result
what happens because of something else
the final effect of a process

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from falling dominoes, then move to the weight of a big decision and to a conclusion you cannot avoid.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从倒下的骨牌开始，再到重大决定的分量，最后到无法回避的结论。

normal.en: Con- is together and sequ- is follow, so a consequence is what follows an act.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，sequ- 是跟随，consequence 就是跟着行为而来的东西。

normal.en: One push on the first domino, and the whole row falls.
normal.cn: 推一下第一张骨牌，整排都会倒下。

normal.en: If you cannot carry the result, do not start the act.
normal.cn: 若你背不起结果，就别开始这个行为。

normal.en: Of little consequence means the thing weighs almost nothing.
normal.cn: of little consequence 意思是这件事几乎没有分量。

normal.en: A sequence is an order; a consequence is the price of that order.
normal.cn: sequence 是顺序，consequence 是这顺序要付的代价。

abstract.en: Picture a line of tiles tipping one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一排骨牌一个接一个倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped into still water.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进平静的水面。

abstract.en: Picture a hand paying a bill it forgot it made.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去付一笔它忘了自己欠下的账。

examples.en: The consequence of the delay was a lost contract.
examples.cn: 这次延误的后果是丢掉了一份合同。

examples.en: He accepted the consequences of his choice.
examples.cn: 他接受了自己选择的后果。

examples.en: The decision was of great consequence to the town.
examples.cn: 这个决定对这座城镇关系重大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consequence 记成 con（一起）加 sequ（跟随）加 ence：紧跟着行为一起到来的那件事，就是后果。

root: 源自拉丁语 consequentia（com 一起 + sequi 跟随），本义是随后而来之物，后指后果、推论与重要性。

sensesIntro.en: From what follows an act, to the weight that makes it matter, and finally to a conclusion forced by facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从随行为而来的东西，到让它有分量的重要性，最后到事实逼出的结论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one push, and the whole row of dominoes falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：推一下，整排骨牌倒下。

branches.en: The core sense is the result that follows an action.
branches.cn: 核心义项是随行为而来的结果。

branches.en: A result with many followers feels important.
branches.cn: 牵动许多后续的结果，就显得重要。

branches.en: In reasoning, the result is a conclusion.
branches.cn: 在推理中，这种结果就是结论。

branches.en: Serious consequences are just results heavy enough to notice.
branches.cn: 严重后果不过是重到让人不得不注意的结果。

branches.en: Both senses deal with weight, one of events and one of logic.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及分量，一个在事件上，一个在逻辑上。

intro.en: Consequence is built on Latin com-, together, plus sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: consequence 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 sequi（跟随）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin follow base sequ- also appears in sequence, sequel and consecutive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的跟随词基 sequ- 也出现在 sequence、sequel 与 consecutive 中。

definition_zh: 替换；代替；替代者；替换物
definition_en: the act of replacing someone or something, or the person or thing that takes their place
core_image: 空出来的工位上，新来的人坐下，桌上的名牌换成了另一个名字
scene: 老队长受伤后，教练从替补席叫上一名球员，这次换人没有打乱阵型。 The replacement slotted into the team without any confusion.
sceneCN: 这里 replacement 是「替补者；替代者」（第 3 个义项：接替他人位置的人）；句意：这名替补顺利融入球队，没有造成混乱。

senses.title: The act of replacing
senses.definition: the act of removing something and putting another thing in its place
senses.definitionCN: 取走某物并在原位放上另一物的动作
senses.example: The replacement of the old windows took two days.
senses.exampleCN: 更换旧窗户花了两天时间。
senses.why: The noun first names the action of the verb replace, with -ment turning the act into a thing you can talk about.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词首先给动词 replace 的动作命名，-ment 把动作变成可以谈论的对象。

senses.title: A thing used instead
senses.definition: a new part or object used in place of one that is broken or old
senses.definitionCN: 用来代替破损或陈旧部件的新零件或新物件
senses.example: The shop ordered a replacement for the damaged screen.
senses.exampleCN: 店里订购了一块屏幕来替换受损的那块。
senses.why: From the act of replacing it is a short step to naming the item that carries the act out.
senses.whyCN: 从替换动作出发，再往前一步就是命名执行替换的那个物件。

senses.title: A person who takes another's place
senses.definition: a person who does someone else's job or fills their position
senses.definitionCN: 接替他人工作或位置的人
senses.example: We need a replacement while she is on leave.
senses.exampleCN: 她休假期间我们需要一名替代者。
senses.why: People, like parts, can be slotted into a role, so the noun extends naturally to human stand-ins.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像零件一样被放进某个角色，所以这个名词自然地扩展到人的替补。

intro.en: Replacement is formed inside English by adding the noun ending -ment to replace.
intro.cn: replacement 是英语内部在 replace 后加名词词尾 -ment 构成的。

items.en: The base place goes back to platea, a broad street or open position.
items.cn: 基础词 place 可上溯到 platea，指宽街或开阔的位置。

items.en: Old French place gives the sense of a spot, role, or room to occupy.
items.cn: 古法语 place 提供「位置、角色或可占据的空间」之意。

items.en: Replace is coined in English from re- and place.
items.cn: replace 是英语用 re- 与 place 创造出来的词。

items.en: The noun replacement appears as the act and result of replacing.
items.cn: 名词 replacement 出现，表示替换的动作及其结果。

items.en: Industrial usage spreads replacement for spare parts and substitute workers.
items.cn: 工业语境使 replacement 广泛用于备用零件和替代工人。

items.en: Modern English also uses it for medical procedures that swap a joint or organ.
items.cn: 现代英语还用它指更换关节或器官的医疗手术。

note.en: Replacement is the noun result of replace, and it is near words for stand-ins and renewals.
note.cn: replacement 是 replace 的名词结果，与表示替补和更新的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Replacement is replace plus -ment, so everything you know about replace transfers, with one extra step: the act becomes a noun.
normalIntro.cn: replacement 就是 replace 加 -ment，关于 replace 的知识都能迁移过来，只多一步：动作变成名词。

normal.en: Add -ment to replace and you get the act or the thing that replaces.
normal.cn: replace 加 -ment，就得到替换的动作或执行替换的东西。

normal.en: A replacement part is a part that fills the same slot.
normal.cn: replacement part 就是填进同一个位置的零件。

normal.en: A replacement player sits ready on the bench.
normal.cn: replacement player 就是坐在替补席上随时准备上场的人。

normal.en: The phrase a replacement for marks what is being swapped out.
normal.cn: a replacement for 标出被替换掉的对象。

normal.en: Irreplaceable means no replacement can be found.
normal.cn: irreplaceable 意为找不到替代者。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate unscrewed and another screwed into the same holes.
abstract.cn: 想象一块名牌被拧下，另一块拧进同样的孔位。

abstract.en: Imagine a substitute runner waiting at the edge of the track.
abstract.cn: 想象一名替补跑者等在跑道边。

abstract.en: Think of a spare part box labelled for the machine it belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴着机器编号的备件盒。

examples.en: The replacement of the roof will start in spring.
examples.cn: 屋顶的更换工程将于春天开始。

examples.en: She ordered a replacement for her broken phone.
examples.cn: 她为坏掉的手机订了一台替代品。

examples.en: The team found a replacement for the injured goalkeeper.
examples.cn: 球队为受伤的门将找到了一名替补。

dict_mnemonic.text: replace（替换）+ -ment（名词词尾）＝替换这件事或替代者；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: replace（替换，由 re- 与 place 构成）+ 名词词尾 -ment，表示替换的行为、被替换上的物件或接替位置的人。

sensesIntro.en: The act comes first, then the object that carries it out, then the person who fills the role.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有替换的动作，再有执行替换的物件，最后是接替位置的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vacant position filled by a new person or part.
core.cn: 核心意象：空出的位置由新的人或零件补上。

branches.en: The act of swapping is the noun's most general sense.
branches.cn: 对换的动作，是这个名词最概括的义项。

branches.en: A replacement can be the part or object that is swapped in.
branches.cn: replacement 也可以指被换上去的零件或物件。

branches.en: A person who fills the role is the human form of the same idea.
branches.cn: 填补角色的人，是同一想法的「人」的形态。

branches.en: The action and the object are inseparable parts of one handover.
branches.cn: 动作与物件是一次交接中不可分割的两部分。

branches.en: Parts and people both slot into a role that must keep running.
branches.cn: 零件和人都会被放进一个必须继续运转的角色。

intro.en: Replacement combines an English verb with a Latin-derived noun ending.
intro.cn: replacement 把一个英语动词与源自拉丁语的名词词尾结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin platea gives place, and the ending -ment comes from Latin -mentum, marking an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 platea 提供 place，词尾 -ment 来自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其结果。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 replace 开头。

items.example: Place is the base of replacement.

definition_en: a large fight between armed forces, or a long hard struggle
core_image: 晨雾中一面倒下的旌旗插在泥地里
scene: 号角在山谷里响起。 The two armies met in battle at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 battle 是「战役」（第 1 个义项：两支武装力量之间的大规模交战）；句意是两支军队在黎明交战。

derivatives.zh: 由 battle 与 field 复合，义为「战场」

senses.title: A fight between armies
senses.definition: a large fight between armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 两支武装力量之间的大规模交战
senses.example: The two armies met in battle at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 两支军队在黎明交战。
senses.why: From Latin battualia, gladiatorial exercises, the word grew into a fight between armies.
senses.whyCN: 从拉丁语 battualia「角斗训练」出发，这个词发展为军队之间的交战。

senses.title: A long hard struggle
senses.definition: a determined effort against a problem or a rival
senses.definitionCN: 针对难题或对手的坚决努力
senses.example: She won her battle against illness.
senses.exampleCN: 她战胜了疾病。
senses.why: The military sense widened to any hard struggle in life.
senses.whyCN: 军事义扩展为生活中任何艰难的奋斗。

senses.title: To fight or struggle

senses.example: They battled the storm all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜与暴风雨搏斗。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to take part in a fight.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示参与战斗。

definition_zh: 最初的；原来的；原创的；原件；原作；真迹的
definition_en: existing from the beginning, newly made and not copied from anything else, or the first version of something from which copies are made
core_image: 一张泛黄的纸从档案盒里被取出，纸边留着折痕，上面是作者亲笔写下的字迹
scene: 老城区的档案馆里，管理员戴着薄手套，把一封旧信从纸盒中取出，信的纸边已经发黄。 The letter in the glass case is an original, not a copy.
sceneCN: 这里的 original 是「原件、原作」（第 3 个义项：作为复制依据的第一份文本或物件）；句意为玻璃柜里的这封信是原件，不是复制品。图中可辨识物件：薄手套、旧信、纸盒。

pos.zh: 最初的；原来的；原创的；真迹的
