senses.title: Existing from the beginning
senses.definition: present at the start of something and not added or changed later
senses.definitionCN: 在某事开始时就已存在，后来既未添加也未改动的
senses.example: The original plan was much simpler than the final one.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的方案比最终方案简单得多。
senses.why: The Latin verb oriri means to rise, so the original thing is the one that stood at the rising point before anything else was laid on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 oriri 意为升起，所以「最初的」那个东西，是站在起点上的那一个，其后的东西都还没有叠加上去。

senses.title: New and not copied from anything else
senses.definition: made by a particular mind rather than taken from an existing work or model
senses.definitionCN: 由某个头脑自己造出，而不是取自已有的作品或样板
senses.example: Her design for the bridge is completely original.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这座桥做的设计完全是原创的。
senses.why: If the source is the beginning, then a work that starts something new is itself a beginning, and the word turns from first in time to first of its kind.
senses.whyCN: 既然源头意味着开始，那么一件开创新东西的作品本身就是一个开始，这个词便从「时间上最早」转成「同类中最早」。

senses.title: The first version from which copies are made
senses.definition: the actual first document, artwork or object that later copies reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 后来各种复制品所依据的第一份真实文件、艺术原作或物件
senses.example: The museum keeps the original of the letter in a dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这封信的原件存放在一间暗室里。
senses.why: A copy needs a point of origin to be measured against, and English gives that first object the adjective as a noun: the original.
senses.whyCN: 复制品需要一个源头来对照，英语干脆把这个形容词当名词用，指那第一件东西：原件。

senses.title: Genuine, not a reproduction
senses.definition: made by the artist or maker themselves rather than produced later by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 由艺术家或制作者本人完成，而不是后人仿制或印刷的
senses.example: The painting on the wall is an original, not a print.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那幅画是真迹，不是印刷品。
senses.why: Once the word marks the first object, it also marks what is real about it: whatever lacks that first hand is only a copy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词标出那第一件东西，它也标出了这件东西的真实之处：凡缺少最初那只手的，就只是复制品。

intro.en: Original goes back to a Latin verb meaning to rise, and its noun for a beginning; the adjective then passed through French into English, where it also became a noun for the first object itself.
intro.cn: original 上溯到拉丁语中意为「升起」的动词及其表示「开始」的名词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来又兼作名词，指那第一件东西本身。

items.en: Oriri meant to rise or to come into being, and it was said of the sun rising as well as of anything that begins.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起、开始存在，既用于太阳升起，也用于任何开始出现的事物。

items.en: The noun origo, with the stem origin-, named a beginning or a source, the point from which a thing rises.
items.cn: 名词 origo 的词干为 origin-，指开端或源头，即事物由之升起的那一点。

items.en: Originalis described what belongs to the beginning or to the source rather than to a later copy.
items.cn: originalis 形容属于开端或源头的东西，而不是属于后来复制品的东西。

items.en: Old French used original for the first form of a thing, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century with that sense.
items.cn: 古法语用 original 指一件事物的最初形态，英语在十四世纪借入时也带来这个意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps original for what comes first in time, for work that is newly made, and for the very object from which copies are taken.
items.cn: 现代英语让 original 兼指时间上最早的、新造而非抄袭的，以及复制所依据的那件实物。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for rising and beginning; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what comes first or is not copied.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「升起、开始」词干上的词；近义组收表示「最早出现」或「非复制」的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Original is an adjective built on the Latin noun for a source, so its hooks follow the moment a thing rises rather than any finished object.
normalIntro.cn: original 是建立在拉丁语「源头」名词上的形容词，所以记忆钩子顺着事物升起的那一刻走，而不是顺着任何成品走。

normal.en: Oriri is the Latin verb to rise, and original names what stood at that rising point before anything else came.
normal.cn: oriri 是拉丁语中表示「升起」的动词，而 original 指在那升起之点上、别的东西尚未到来时就已经存在的那一个。

normal.en: Origin is the noun of the same verb, and original is its adjective, so the pair keeps one stem in origin-.
normal.cn: origin 是同一动词的名词，original 是它的形容词，两者共用一个词干 origin-。

normal.en: The ending -al means belonging to, so original literally means belonging to the origin.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 表示「属于……的」，所以 original 字面上就是「属于源头的」。

normal.en: The original meaning of a word is its oldest sense, while an original idea is one nobody had before, and the same word covers both kinds of first.
normal.cn: the original meaning 指一个词最老的义项，而 an original idea 指没人想到过的想法，同一个词兼指两种「第一」。

normal.en: An original painting is not a print because the word insists on the first object, not on the many copies made after it.
normal.cn: an original painting 不是印刷品，因为这个词强调的是第一件东西，而不是其后做出的许多复制品。

abstract.en: A word for the moment of rising suggests that originality is not decoration but a beginning someone had to make.
abstract.cn: 一个指向「升起那一刻」的词说明：原创不是装饰，而是有人必须做出的一个开端。

abstract.en: Every copy quietly points back to an original, even when nobody remembers who made the first one.
abstract.cn: 每一件复制品都默默指向一个原件，即便没人记得第一件是谁做的。

abstract.en: First in time and first of its kind are two different honours, and English lets one word carry both.
abstract.cn: 时间上的最早与同类中的首创是两种不同的光荣，而英语让一个词同时承担。

definition_zh: 代理机构；代理公司；中介；（政府）机构；能动性；中介作用；代理权
definition_en: a business or organization that provides a service for others, an official body with a particular duty, or the power and means of acting
core_image: 一只手把另一只手引到台前：事情由别人代你去办
scene: 凌晨的编辑部里，记者把刚写好的稿子交给通讯社的值班员。 The news agency sent the story to every member paper.
sceneCN: 这里 agency 是「代理机构、通讯社」（第 1 个义项：替别人提供服务并代为发布的机构）；句意为这家通讯社把这篇报道发给了每一家成员报纸。画面里是夜间的编辑部、成排的稿纸与值班电话。

pos.zh: 名词：代理机构；政府机构；能动性；代理权

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「代理的；施动的」
由本词加前缀 inter- 构成，义为「跨机构的；机构之间的」
由本词加前缀 sub- 构成，义为「分代理处；分社」

senses.title: A business that acts for clients
senses.definition: a business that provides a particular service for other people or companies
senses.definitionCN: 为其他人或公司提供某项服务的商业机构
senses.example: She booked the flights through a travel agency.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过一家旅行社订了机票。
senses.why: Latin agere means to do or drive, and this noun names the office where the doing is carried out on someone else's behalf: the client hands the action over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做、驱动」，这个名词指「替别人做事的办事处」：委托人把「做」这件事交了出去。

senses.title: An official body of the state
senses.definition: an official organization, often part of a government, with a particular duty
senses.definitionCN: 承担某项专门职责的官方组织，常为政府的一部分
senses.example: The environmental agency ordered tests of the river water.
senses.exampleCN: 环保机构下令检测河水。
senses.why: A public body is also an office of doing: the state sets up a unit whose entire job is to carry out one kind of action.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构同样是「办事的处所」：国家设立一个单位，它的全部工作就是执行某一类行动。

senses.title: The capacity to act
senses.definition: the capacity of a person or group to act and make choices, especially in social science
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体行动并作出选择的能力，尤用于社会科学
senses.example: The study asks how much agency tenants have in shaping housing policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追问租户在影响住房政策上有多少能动性。
senses.why: Take the office away and what is left is the bare capacity to do; this abstract sense is agere turned into a noun with no institution attached.
senses.whyCN: 把「办事处」这层机构拿走，剩下的就是「做」的能力；这个抽象义就是 agere 变成名词后不再挂靠任何机构。

senses.title: Action through a means
senses.definition: the means by which something is done, especially in the formal phrase by the agency of
senses.definitionCN: 某事得以完成所凭借的手段，尤用于正式短语 by the agency of
senses.example: The disease spread by the agency of contaminated water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病经由受污染的水传播。
senses.why: When one thing produces an effect, it acts as the doer for another, so the word comes to mean the channel through which an effect is carried.
senses.whyCN: 当一样东西产生某种效果时，它就替另一方充当了「执行者」，于是这个词也指效果借以传出的通道。

senses.title: The authority to represent another
senses.definition: the position, authority or business of representing another person or company
senses.definitionCN: 代表另一个人或公司行事的职位、权限或业务
senses.example: The firm holds an agency for three European brands.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司持有三个欧洲品牌的代理权。
senses.why: Behind the institution lies a legal arrangement: one party is authorised to act for another, which is exactly what agere means in legal Latin.
senses.whyCN: 机构背后是一种法律安排：一方获准替另一方行事，这正是法律拉丁语里 agere 的意思。

intro.en: Agency is the abstract noun of a Latin verb for doing, carried into English through French; the office and the capacity to act come from the same stem.
intro.cn: agency 是拉丁语中表示「做」的动词的抽象名词，经法语进入英语；「机构」与「行动能力」出自同一个词干。

items.en: Agere meant 'to do, drive, set in motion'; its present participle agens, stem agent-, named the one who does.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使动起来」；它的现在分词 agens 词干为 agent-，用来指「做事的人」。

items.en: The late Latin noun agentia meant 'action, doing' and also 'the office of one who acts for another'; it is recorded, not reconstructed.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语名词 agentia 表示「行动、做事」，也指「代为行事者的职务」；它有文献记录，不是重构形式。

items.en: French agence carried the word towards English with the sense of an office or a way of acting.
items.cn: 法语 agence 把这个词带向英语，带有「办事处」与「行事方式」的意思。

items.en: The commercial sense 'a business acting for clients' is recorded from the seventeenth century; the philosophical sense 'capacity to act' is far later, and exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 「替客户办事的商业机构」这一义项自十七世纪起有记录；「行动能力」的哲学义出现得晚得多，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Government agencies, news agencies and the abstract talk of human agency now sit side by side, all from the same verb of doing.
items.cn: 政府机构、通讯社与关于人的能动性的抽象讨论如今并存，全都出自同一个表示「做」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same Latin verb of doing, plus one noun that merely rhymes in spelling; the near-meaning group holds institutions and words for the power to act.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「做」动词的词族，另收一个只是拼写相像的名词；近义组收机构类词与表示行动能力的词。

entries.definition: The person who acts for another, built directly on the Latin participle stem agent-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人」，直接由拉丁分词词干 agent- 构成，是 agency 的同根词。

entries.definition: A list of things to be done, from a Latin form of the same verb agere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「议程、待办事项」，来自同一个动词 agere 的拉丁形式，本义是「该做的事」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to action, formed from agency with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理的、施动的」，由 agency 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: The state of needing immediate attention; only its ending looks like agency, and it comes from a Latin verb meaning to press.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「紧急、急迫」；只是词尾与 agency 相近，词源不同，来自表示「压、催」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: An office or a department, especially a government one; it names the room rather than the delegated action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「办事处、局」，多指政府部门；它强调的是办公场所，而不是被托付的行动。

entries.definition: An established organization or custom; broader than agency and not limited to service work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度」，比 agency 更宽，不限于服务性工作。

entries.definition: A business company; commercial in tone and silent about whether it acts for clients.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司、商行」，语气偏商业，不说明是否替客户办事。

entries.definition: The ability to act first without being told; close to the abstract sense of agency but personal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主动性、首创精神」，接近 agency 的抽象义，但更强调个人的主动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb agere and the everyday compounds the word forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 agere，以及这个词构成的各种日常复合形式。

normal.en: Agere is to do; an agent is the one who does, and an agency is the office where the doing happens.
normal.cn: agere 是「做」；agent 是做事的人，agency 是做事的那间办公室。

normal.en: A travel agency does the booking so that you do not have to stand in the queue.
normal.cn: travel agency 替你把票订好，你不必自己去排队。

normal.en: A news agency does the gathering and sends the result to papers that cannot be everywhere.
normal.cn: news agency 替人跑现场，再把结果发给无法到处派人的报纸。

normal.en: By the agency of means through the working of something, as in a disease carried by water.
normal.cn: by the agency of 意为「借助某物的作用」，例如经由水传播的疾病。

normal.en: Human agency is simply people's own power to do something about their situation.
normal.cn: human agency 就是人自己动手改变处境的能力。

abstract.en: One hand guides another hand to sign: the signature is real, but the acting hand belongs to someone else.
abstract.cn: 一只手引着另一只手签字：签名是真的，动的那只手却属于别人。

abstract.en: A switchboard connecting a call: the caller and the answerer never touch, yet the connection is the work.
abstract.cn: 总机把一通电话接上：主叫与被叫从不接触，而接通本身就是那份工作。

abstract.en: A stand-in on a stage: the body is visible, the authority is borrowed.
abstract.cn: 舞台上的替身：身体看得见，权限却是借来的。

examples.en: We rented the flat through a local agency.
examples.cn: 我们通过当地一家中介租下了这套公寓。

examples.en: Two government agencies are investigating the spill.
examples.cn: 两个政府机构正在调查这次泄漏。

examples.en: Children need room to exercise their own agency.
examples.cn: 孩子需要空间去行使自己的能动性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶珍西」——诶，珍西替你把事情办了：代理机构。

root: 拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」的现在分词词干 agent- 加名词后缀构成晚期拉丁语 agentia「行动、办事、代理职务」，经法语 agence 进入英语；核心始终是「替人行事」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of agency all come from one verb of doing: a business that does for clients, a state body that does one kind of work, the bare capacity to do, the channel through which an effect is done, and the legal right to do for another.
sensesIntro.cn: agency 的五个义项都出自同一个表示「做」的动词：替客户做事的商号、专做一类事的国家机构、单纯的做事能力、效果借以传出的通道，以及替他人行事的法定权限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand guides another hand to sign a document.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手引着另一只手在文件上签字。

branches.en: SERVICE: the office where the doing is done for paying clients.
branches.cn: 服务线：替付费客户做事的那个办事处。

branches.en: STATE: the same office, set up by government to carry out one kind of action.
branches.cn: 国家线：同一个办事处，由政府设立，专做一类行动。

branches.en: CAPACITY: the institution removed, leaving only the power to act.
branches.cn: 能力线：把机构拿走，只剩下行动的力量。

branches.en: CHANNEL: one thing doing for another, so the word means the means by which an effect travels.
branches.cn: 通道线：一样东西替另一样起作用，于是这个词指效果传递所凭借的手段。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: the legal right that lets one party act in the name of another.
branches.cn: 权限线：让一方以另一方名义行事的法定权利。

intro.en: Agency is a Latin verb stem plus abstract endings, with English prefixes and suffixes extending the family.
intro.cn: agency 是拉丁动词词干加抽象名词词尾，英语再用前缀与后缀扩展这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Agere, agens and agentia are all recorded in Latin; no form in this family is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere、agens、agentia 在拉丁语中都有记录，这个词族里没有重构形式。

items.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion
items.example: It is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: Its stem agent- names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干 agent- 用来指做事的人。

items.example: It opens both agent and agency.
items.exampleCN: 它同时是 agent 与 agency 的开头。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: It turns the participle stem into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词词干变成名词。

items.example: It gives the modern ending of agency.
items.exampleCN: 它给出 agency 的现代词尾。

definition_en: very strict or harsh, very serious or dangerous, or plain and without decoration
core_image: 暴雨砸在窗上，树枝被风压得几乎折断
scene: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。 The storm caused severe damage.
sceneCN: 这里 severe 是「严峻的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

senses.title: Strict and harsh
senses.definition: very strict or harsh in treatment or judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在对待或评判上非常严格、苛刻的
senses.example: The judge gave a severe warning.
senses.exampleCN: 法官给出了严厉的警告。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义。

senses.title: Very serious
senses.definition: very serious or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重或危险的
senses.example: The storm caused severe damage.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。
senses.why: Danger is strict in its own way.
senses.whyCN: 危险也有它自己的严厉。

senses.title: Plain and simple
senses.definition: plain and without decoration
senses.definitionCN: 朴素、不加装饰的
senses.example: The room was clean and severe.
senses.exampleCN: 房间干净而朴素。
senses.why: A severe style allows nothing extra.
senses.whyCN: 朴素的风格不允许任何多余。

intro.en: Severe comes from Latin severus, serious and strict, through Old French.
intro.cn: severe 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Severus meant serious and strict.
items.cn: severus 意为严肃而严格。

items.en: Severitas named strictness.
items.cn: severitas 指严格。

items.en: Severe meant harsh or strict.
items.cn: severe 意为严厉或严格。

items.en: Severe described strict judgment.
items.cn: severe 描述严格的评判。

items.en: Severe extended to serious conditions and plain style.
items.cn: severe 扩展到严峻的状况与朴素的风格。

note.en: Severe is compared with similar-looking words and with words for harshness.
note.cn: 把 severe 与形近词以及表示严厉的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Severe is a line drawn hard: strict rules, serious harm, plain style.
normalIntro.cn: severe 是一条画得很硬的线：严格的规则、严重的伤害、朴素的风格。

normal.en: The drought was severe.
normal.cn: 旱情很严重。

normal.en: He felt severe pain in his back.
normal.cn: 他背部剧痛。

normal.en: The school has severe rules.
normal.cn: 这所学校规定严厉。

normal.en: The building has a severe design.
normal.cn: 这栋建筑设计朴素。

normal.en: The severest winter in years came.
normal.cn: 多年来最严酷的冬天来了。

abstract.en: A severe line cuts away everything unnecessary.
abstract.cn: 严厉的线条，会削去一切多余。

abstract.en: What is serious cannot be softened by ignoring it.
abstract.cn: 严重的事，不能靠忽视来减轻。

abstract.en: Plainness can be a kind of strength.
abstract.cn: 朴素，也可以是一种力量。

examples.en: The storm caused severe damage.
examples.cn: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

examples.en: The judge gave a severe warning.
examples.cn: 法官给出了严厉的警告。

examples.en: The room was clean and severe.
examples.cn: 房间干净而朴素。

dict_mnemonic.text: severe 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），核心义「不留余地的严」，引申为严重与朴素。

root: 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），核心义「毫不宽松」。

sensesIntro.en: Severe means strict, very serious, or plain and undecorated.
sensesIntro.cn: severe 意为严厉的、严峻的或朴素的。

core.en: A quality that allows no softness or excess.
core.cn: 不容松懈、不容多余的特质。

branches.en: Strict treatment or judgment.
branches.cn: 严格的处理或评判。

branches.en: A situation that is very bad.
branches.cn: 非常糟糕的处境。

branches.en: A style without decoration.
branches.cn: 不加装饰的风格。

branches.en: Harshness in people and in events.
branches.cn: 人和事件中的严酷。

branches.en: Serious conditions and plain forms both cut away ease.
branches.cn: 严峻的处境与朴素的形式，都削去了安逸。

intro.en: Severe is a Latin adjective whose family includes severity and persevere.
intro.cn: severe 是拉丁语形容词，其词族包括 severity 与 persevere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin severus, serious, also lies behind persevere, to persist strictly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 severus（严肃）也是 persevere（严格坚持）的词源基础。

items.example: This winter is severer than last.
items.exampleCN: 这个冬天比去年更严酷。

items.example: It was the severest test of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这是全年最严峻的考验。

items.example: The severity of the storm surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨的猛烈让我们吃惊。

items.example: The severeness of his tone was clear.

items.exampleCN: 尽管遭遇挫折，她仍坚持不懈。
